paras.en: Billie Eilish and Finneas have made plenty of hits together, but their latest collaboration is something you can actually wear.
paras.zh: Billie Eilish 和 Finneas 合作过很多热门作品，但他们最新的合作作品却是你可以实际穿着的单品。

paras.en: The Grammy-winning siblings have teamed up with John Hardy for their first co-designed jewelry collection, available as of Wednesday, Oct. 21, at JohnHardy.com, John Hardy stores and select retailers. The collection features rings, necklaces, bracelets and earrings that reflect their very different approaches to personal style.
paras.zh: 格莱美奖得主兄弟姐妹与 John Hardy 合作推出了他们的首个共同设计的珠宝系列，该系列将于 10 月 21 日星期三在 JohnHardy.com、John Hardy 商店和精选零售商处发售。该系列包括戒指、项链、手镯和耳环，反映了他们截然不同的个人风格。

paras.en: The lineup is split into two distinct styles. Wildflower, named after Eilish’s Grammy-winning song from Hit Me Hard and Soft, takes a softer approach with sterling silver flowers, delicate pendants and lab-grown diamonds. There’s even a triple ring stack that brings three floral designs together, plus threader earrings that can be worn through multiple piercings.
paras.zh: 该阵容分为两种不同的风格。 Wildflower 以艾利什 (Eilish) 的《Hit Me Hard and Soft》中的格莱美获奖歌曲命名，采用纯银花朵、精致的吊坠和实验室制造的钻石，采用更柔和的风格。甚至还有将三种花卉设计融合在一起的三重戒指叠层，以及可以穿过多个穿孔佩戴的穿线耳环。

paras.en: Screwball, meanwhile, is where things get a little edgier. Chunky chain necklaces, sculptural bracelets and piercing-inspired hardware bring an industrial feel to the collection, offering a contrast to Wildflower’s more delicate designs.
paras.zh: 与此同时，事情变得有点紧张。粗链项链、雕塑手链和穿孔金属配件为该系列带来工业感，与 Wildflower 更精致的设计形成鲜明对比。

paras.en: And this wasn’t a case of simply putting two famous names on a jewelry collection. The siblings spent the past year working closely with John Hardy’s New York and Bali design teams, helping develop the pieces from initial concepts to finished designs. Sustainability also played a role, with reclaimed metals and lab-grown diamonds incorporated into the collection.
paras.zh: 这并不是简单地将两个著名名字放在一个珠宝系列上的情况。过去一年，兄弟姐妹与约翰·哈迪 (John Hardy) 的纽约和巴厘岛设计团队密切合作，帮助开发从最初概念到最终设计的作品。可持续性也发挥了作用，回收金属和实验室制造的钻石融入到该系列中。

paras.en: “Jewelry has always been an enormous part of how I express myself,” Eilish said in a statement. “In my current day to day, I wear daintier jewelry. On tour, I love a chunkier, thicker piece. I love that we were able to work with both styles.”
paras.zh: “珠宝一直是我表达自我的重要组成部分，”艾利什在一份声明中说道。 “在我现在的日常生活中，我佩戴更精致的珠宝。在巡演中，我喜欢更厚实的珠宝。我喜欢我们能够同时使用这两种风格。”

paras.en: BILLIE EILISH & FINNEAS X JH Wildflower Stud Earrings
paras.zh: BILLIE EILISH & FINNEAS X JH 野花耳钉

paras.en: These sterling silver studs feature carved petals that give the floral design a three-dimensional look. They’re part of the Wildflower collection, inspired by Eilish’s Grammy-winning song of the same name.
paras.zh: 这些纯银耳钉带有雕刻花瓣，为花卉设计带来三维外观。它们是 Wildflower 系列的一部分，灵感来自 Eilish 的格莱美获奖同名歌曲。

paras.en: BILLIE EILISH & FINNEAS X JH Wildflower Stacking Rings Set of 3
paras.zh: BILLIE EILISH & FINNEAS X JH 野花叠戴戒指 3 件套

paras.en: This isn’t your typical matching ring set. Each of the three sterling silver bands has a different sculpted flower design, allowing you to stack them together or mix them with other jewelry.
paras.zh: 这不是典型的配套戒指套装。三个纯银戒指均具有不同的雕刻花朵设计，您可以将它们堆叠在一起或与其他珠宝混合。

paras.en: BILLIE EILISH & FINNEAS X JH Screwball Link Bracelet
paras.zh: BILLIE EILISH & FINNEAS X JH 螺丝球链接手链

paras.en: Part of the Screwball lineup, this $695 bracelet pairs sculptural silver links with an industrial-inspired silhouette. It’s handcrafted from reclaimed sterling silver and finished with a lobster clasp.
paras.zh: 这款售价 695 美元的手链是 Screwball 系列的一部分，将雕塑般的银链与工业风格的轮廓搭配在一起。它采用回收的纯银手工制成，并配有龙虾扣。

paras.en: The launch also gives “Wildflower” another moment in the spotlight. The track appears on Eilish’s Hit Me Hard and Soft, which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and also produced the Billboard Hot 100 hit “Birds of a Feather.” Eilish performed “Wildflower” throughout her Hit Me Hard and Soft world tour, which wrapped in November 2025.
paras.zh: 此次发布也让《野花》再次成为人们关注的焦点。这首歌出现在 Eilish 的《Hit Me Hard and Soft》中，该歌曲在 Billboard 200 排行榜上名列第二，并且还制作了 Billboard Hot 100 热门单曲“Birds of a Feather”。艾利什在她于 2025 年 11 月结束的 Hit Me Hard and Soft 世界巡演中演奏了《Wildflower》。

articles.title: The Offspring Guitarist Noodles Stepping Away From Live Performance Due to ‘Fairly Serious Health Issue’
articles.author: Gil Kaufman

paras.en: The Offspring guitarist and co-founder Noodles announced on Wednesday morning (Oct. 21) that he is stepping back from the band’s tour to deal with a health issue. In a statement posted on Instagram, the 63-year-old punk veteran wrote, “It is with deep sadness that I have to announce that I need to step away from live performance for a while to deal with a sudden and fairly serious health issue.”
paras.zh: Offspring 吉他手兼联合创始人 Noodles 于周三上午（10 月 21 日）宣布，由于健康问题，他将退出乐队巡演。这位 63 岁的朋克老手在 Instagram 上发布的一份声明中写道：“我非常悲伤地宣布，我需要暂时停止现场表演，以应对突然出现的相当严重的健康问题。”

paras.en: At press time, a spokesperson for the group had not returned Billboard‘s request for additional details on what is ailing the musician born Kevin John Wasserman, how long he expected to be absent from the group’s live lineup and who will replace him for a run of upcoming gigs in support of their 11th studio album, 2024’s Supercharged.
paras.zh: 截至发稿时，该乐队的发言人尚未回复 Billboard 的请求，要求提供更多详细信息，包括出生于音乐人 Kevin John Wasserman 的病情、他预计将缺席乐队现场阵容多久，以及谁将接替他参加即将举行的一系列演出，以支持他们的第 11 张录音室专辑《2024 年的 Supercharged》。

paras.en: Noodles assured fans that his Orange County, Calif.-bred bandmates support him during this difficult time.
paras.zh: 面条向歌迷保证，他在加利福尼亚州奥兰治县出生的乐队成员会在这段困难时期支持他。

paras.en: “The rest of the band has my back, is super supportive, and will keep rocking you all in my absence,” he said. “I hope to be back on stage sooner rather than later. Until then, I will miss all of you with all of my heart. Thanks for keeping me in your thoughts. I really appreciate it.”
paras.zh: “乐队的其他成员都支持我，非常支持我，在我不在的时候他们会继续震撼你们所有人，”他说。 “我希望早点回到舞台。在那之前，我会全心全意地想念你们所有人。谢谢你们一直惦记着我。我真的很感激。”

paras.en: Noodles also got plenty of support from his pop punk brethren, including Simple Plan singer Pierre Bouvier, who wrote, “Hope you’re ok brother. Sending love and positivity. You’re a legend…. You got this. ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️,” and well wishes from Slightly Stoopid, The Early November and Sublime, among others.
paras.zh: Noodles 也得到了他的流行朋克弟兄们的大力支持，包括 Simple Plan 歌手 Pierre Bouvier，他写道：“兄弟，希望你一切都好。传递爱和积极性。你是一个传奇......你得到了。❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️”，以及来自 Slightly Stoopid、The Early October 和 Sublime 等人的良好祝愿。

paras.en: The Offspring have been on the road all year on their Supercharged tour, with upcoming dates booked on Saturday (Oct. 24) at the Wiltern in Los Angeles, as well as SEMA Fest in Las Vegas on Nov. 6 and the Corona Capital 2026 festival in Mexico City on Nov. 21. After that, they will take a break from the road until a Jan. 16 show at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles as part of the iHeartRadio ALTer Ego 2027 festival.
paras.zh: Offspring 全年都在路上进行他们的 Supercharged 巡演，预定了周六（10 月 24 日）在洛杉矶 Wiltern 举行的即将到来的日期，以及 11 月 6 日在拉斯维加斯举行的 SEMA Fest 和 11 月 21 日在墨西哥城举行的 Corona Capital 2026 音乐节。之后，他们将在旅途中休息一下，直到 1 月 16 日作为 iHeartRadio ALTer Ego 的一部分在洛杉矶 Kia Forum 进行演出。 2027 年节日。

articles.title: Oops! How Danny Trejo Accidentally Made a Pro-ICE Movie
articles.author: Lexy Perez

paras.en: Danny Trejo has played a Mexican revolutionary, a Mexican cop, a Mexican cartel assassin and, of course, a Mexican ex-con who kills bad guys with a machete. One time, in a 2015 Super Bowl ad for Snickers, he even played a Mexican Marcia Brady. But now, after more than 400 screen appearances, the 82-year-old actor has popped up in a part nobody
paras.zh: 丹尼·特乔扮演过一名墨西哥革命者、一名墨西哥警察、一名墨西哥卡特尔刺客，当然还有一名用砍刀杀死坏人的墨西哥前科犯。有一次，在士力架 2015 年超级碗广告中，他甚至扮演了墨西哥人玛西娅·布雷迪 (Marcia Brady)。但现在，在出演了 400 多次银幕后，这位 82 岁的演员突然出现在一个无人问津的角色中。

paras.en: saw coming, not even Trejo: He’s the Mexican star of a pro-ICE movie.
paras.zh: 就连特雷乔也预见到了他的到来：他是一部支持 ICE 的电影中的墨西哥明星。

paras.en: Last month, Trejo finished filming Pawn Shop, an action-thriller in which he portrays the owner of a Minneapolis store that becomes ground zero for a standoff involving ICE, anti-ICE protesters, Antifa and MS-13 gang members. While Rambling Reporter can’t definitively confirm the online rumors about how the film is chock-full of offensive anti-immigration agitprop — we haven’t read the script, only heard what’s in it, including a scene involving an unhinged, COVID mask-wearing agitator blaring NPR on her radio while mowing down ICE agents with her SUV — it’s not hard to imagine Stephen Miller in the front row, hugging a big bucket of popcorn.
paras.zh: 上个月，特雷霍完成了《当铺》的拍摄，这是一部动作惊悚片，他在片中饰演明尼阿波利斯一家商店的老板，该商店因 ICE、反 ICE 抗议者、Antifa 和 MS-13 帮派成员之间的对峙而沦为归零地。虽然漫漫记者无法明确证实网上有关这部电影充满攻击性反移民煽动性的谣言——我们还没有读过剧本，只听过其中的内容，其中包括一个戴着新冠面具的精神错乱的煽动者在收音机里大声播放 NPR 的场景，同时用她的 SUV 砍倒 ICE 特工——不难想象史蒂芬·米勒坐在前排，抱着一大桶爆米花。

paras.en: Trejo declined to talk to Rambling, but a source close to the production says he had no idea the film was being produced by Ben Shapiro’s Daily Wire, the conservative media company behind such MAGA-leaning pictures as the 2023 anti-trans comedy Lady Ballers. “They called [Trejo] and said, ‘Hey, we got this movie — you’d play a pawnshop owner and there’s this huge protest and a clash with ICE. And he was like, ‘OK, cool, send me my lines,’ ” says the source.
paras.zh: 特雷霍拒绝接受 Rambling 的采访，但一位接近制片的消息人士表示，他不知道这部电影是由本·夏皮罗的《每日电讯报》制作的，该公司是一家保守的媒体公司，制作了 2023 年反跨性别喜剧《Lady Ballers》等倾向 MAGA 的影片。 “他们打电话给[Trejo]并说，‘嘿，我们拍了这部电影——你将扮演一名当铺老板，发生了巨大的抗议活动，并与 ICE 发生了冲突。他说，‘好吧，酷，把我的台词发给我，’”消息人士说。

paras.en: As it happens, this isn’t the first time Trejo has wandered unwittingly into Shapiro-land. In 2024, he voiced a character on the Daily Wire’s anti-woke cartoon Mr. Birchum, a gig he took simply because he knew series creator Adam Carolla. But Pawn Shop is considerably harder to mistake for just another acting job. Protesters began showing up at the set — where swarms of extras were playing protesters — and Trejo eventually began pushing back on his lines. “He couldn’t walk off the movie — he’d get sued,” says the source. “But he made them change a bunch of stuff. He was like, ‘No, I’m not going to say that.’”
paras.zh: 碰巧的是，这并不是特雷霍第一次无意中误入夏皮罗的土地。 2024 年，他为《每日电讯报》的反觉醒卡通片《伯彻姆先生》中的一个角色配音，他参加这个角色只是因为他认识该剧的创作者亚当·卡罗拉。但当铺很难被误认为是另一项表演工作。抗议者开始出现在片场——那里有一大群临时演员扮演抗议者——特雷霍最终开始反击他的台词。 “他不能离开这部电影——他会被起诉，”消息人士说。 “但他让他们改变了很多东西。他说，‘不，我不会这么说。’”

paras.en: Is John Travolta writing another memoir? THR investigates. Amanda Seyfried is a bit tongue-tied on red carpets these days but happy to talk about emus.
paras.zh: 约翰·特拉沃尔塔正在写另一本回忆录吗？ THR 正在进行调查。阿曼达·塞弗里德（Amanda Seyfried）这些天在红地毯上有点张口结舌，但很高兴谈论鸸鹋。

articles.title: Is John Travolta Writing a Memoir (Again)?
articles.author: Andy Lewis

paras.en: Rambling hears rumors that John Travolta, 72, is shopping a memoir, some 20 years after his last attempt at an auto-biography mysteriously vanished before it reached bookstores. Back in 2004, Travolta signed a blockbuster book deal — reportedly $2.5 million for U.S. rights and another $2.3 million for the U.K. — with a pub date set for the fall of 2006. “I’ve hit a milestone this year in my life, turning 50,” the actor said at the time. “If I waited any longer, I’d have to write two books.”
paras.zh: Ramble 听说 72 岁的约翰·特拉沃尔塔 (John Travolta) 正在购买一本回忆录，大约 20 年前，他最后一次尝试写自传，但在到达书店之前就神秘消失了。早在 2004 年，特拉沃尔塔就签署了一项轰动一时的图书交易——据报道，美国版权为 250 万美元，英国版权为 230 万美元——出版日期定于 2006 年秋季。“今年我已经 50 岁了，这是我人生中的一个里程碑，”这位演员当时说道。 “如果我再等下去，我就得写两本书了。”

paras.en: If Travolta is indeed giving a memoir another shot, he couldn’t have picked a better time for it. Celebrity autobiographies are on fire these days — Michael Douglas, Sylvester Stallone, Kyle MacLachlan, Ari Emanuel, they’re all elbowing one another on best-seller lists. Travolta would be “a get,” notes one veteran publishing executive, adding that the actor is “still beloved, even with all the Scientology nonsense.”
paras.zh: 如果特拉沃尔塔确实要再次尝试写一本回忆录，那么他不可能选择更好的时机了。如今，名人自传很火——迈克尔·道格拉斯、西尔维斯特·史泰龙、凯尔·麦克拉克伦、阿里·伊曼纽尔，他们都在畅销书排行榜上争先恐后。一位资深出版主管指出，特拉沃尔塔将是“一个受欢迎的人”，并补充说，这位演员“仍然受到人们的喜爱，即使有那么多山达基派的废话。”

paras.en: Back in 2004, Hyperion’s then-editor-in-chief Will Schwalbe promised Travolta’s memoir would “surprise, move and entertain readers on every page” with stories about Travolta’s “many notable friendships,” including Marlon Brando and Princess Diana. The untitled project got far enough in Hyperion’s pipeline to be assigned an ISBN and listed in bookseller databases as a 384-page hardcover.
paras.zh: 早在 2004 年，Hyperion 时任主编威尔·施瓦尔贝 (Will Schwalbe) 就曾承诺，特拉沃尔塔的回忆录将“在每一页上给读者带来惊喜、感动和娱乐”，讲述特拉沃尔塔“许多著名的友谊”的故事，其中包括马龙·白兰度和戴安娜王妃。这个未命名的项目在 Hyperion 的管道中取得了足够的进展，被分配了 ISBN，并作为 384 页的精装本在书商数据库中列出。

paras.en: Exactly what happened to the memoir, why Travolta abandoned it and what became of his advance remain a mystery. But plenty has happened in the 22 years since he first proposed telling his life story, much of it painful, including the death of his 16-year-old son, Jett, following a seizure in 2009, and wife Kelly Preston’s death from breast cancer in 2020. It turns out Travolta really does have enough material for two books. Maybe one of them will even make it into bookstores.
paras.zh: 这本回忆录究竟发生了什么，特拉沃尔塔为何放弃它，以及他的进展如何仍然是个谜。但自从他第一次提出讲述自己的人生故事以来，22 年来发生了很多事情，其中​​大部分都是痛苦的，包括 2009 年他 16 岁的儿子杰特 (Jett) 因癫痫发作去世，以及 2020 年妻子凯莉·普雷斯顿 (Kelly Preston) 因乳腺癌去世。事实证明，特拉沃尔塔确实有足够的材料写两本书。也许其中之一甚至会进入书店。

paras.en: Amanda Seyfried is a bit tongue-tied on red carpets these days but happy to talk about emus. Danny Trejo stars in Pawn Shop, a controversial film tied to ICE protests.
paras.zh: 阿曼达·塞弗里德（Amanda Seyfried）这些天在红地毯上有点张口结舌，但很高兴谈论鸸鹋。丹尼·特乔 (Danny Trejo) 主演了《当铺》(Pawn Shop)，这是一部与 ICE 抗议活动有关的争议电影。

articles.title: Amanda Seyfried Would Rather Talk About Emus
articles.author: Lexy Perez

paras.en: Amanda Seyfried’s fans were not happy with the questions she was getting on the red carpet at the Academy Museum Gala on Oct. 17. “I don’t like this reporter,” complained one commenter after video of the exchange hit social media. “This is so unfair to her,” wrote another. “Who asks someone trying to keep their shit together these kinds of questions!!” demanded a third.
paras.zh: 阿曼达·塞弗里德 (Amanda Seyfried) 的粉丝对她 10 月 17 日在学院博物馆晚会上在红地毯上接受的问题并不满意。“我不喜欢这个记者，”在这场交流的视频在社交媒体上流传后，一位评论者抱怨道。另一位网友写道：“这对她来说太不公平了。” “谁会问一个试图把自己的狗屎放在一起的人这些问题！！”要求第三个。

paras.en: Given that Seyfried and husband Thomas Sadoski recently announced they were separating after nine years of marriage, plenty of viewers assumed they knew what she was being asked about.
paras.zh: 鉴于塞弗里德和丈夫托马斯·萨多斯基最近宣布他们在结婚九年后分居，许多观众认为他们知道她被问到了什么。

paras.en: They didn’t. In fact, the slightly surreal conversation unfolding on the carpet had nothing to do with Seyfried’s personal life. It concerned something going on in her professional life that she can’t talk about yet. We know what it is. She knows we know what it is. But telling you what it is would spoil the surprise, so we’re not going to. (Suffice it to say, it has something to do with a just-released documentary about a certain black-turtlenecked Silicon Valley huckster whom Seyfried once played on television.)
paras.zh: 他们没有。事实上，地毯上展开的略显超现实的对话与塞弗里德的个人生活无关。这涉及到她职业生涯中发生的一些事情，但她目前还不能谈论。我们知道它是什么。她知道我们知道那是什么。但告诉你它是什么会破坏惊喜，所以我们不会。 （可以这么说，这与刚刚发布的一部纪录片有关，该纪录片讲述了塞弗里德曾经在电视上扮演的某个黑色高领硅谷小贩的故事。）

paras.en: Seyfried acknowledged that it was “really hard to do interviews right now,” although “for good reason.” Asked what people could safely talk to her about, she suggested emus, Halloween, apple pie, olives and “really good hard ciders.” To anyone unaware of the other thing going on in Seyfried’s life, however, the exchange looked remarkably like a reporter trying to coax a newly separated actress into discussing her marriage while she desperately tried to change the subject.
paras.zh: 塞弗里德承认，“现在进行采访确实很困难”，尽管“有充分的理由”。当被问及人们可以安全地与她谈论什么时，她建议鸸鹋、万圣节、苹果派、橄榄和“非常好的烈性苹果酒”。然而，对于那些不知道塞弗里德生活中发生的其他事情的人来说，这次交流看起来非常像一名记者试图哄骗一位刚刚分居的女演员讨论她的婚姻，而她则拼命试图改变话题。

paras.en: Even Seyfried seemed amused by the confusion. After watching the clip, she left a comment of her own: “What AM I even saying.”
paras.zh: 就连塞弗里德也似乎对这种混乱感到好笑。看完视频后，她留下了自己的评论：“我到底在说什么。”

paras.en: Is John Travolta writing another memoir? THR investigates. Danny Trejo stars in Pawn Shop, a controversial film tied to ICE protests.
paras.zh: 约翰·特拉沃尔塔正在写另一本回忆录吗？ THR 正在进行调查。丹尼·特乔 (Danny Trejo) 主演了《当铺》(Pawn Shop)，这是一部与 ICE 抗议活动有关的争议电影。

articles.title: How Ukraine’s drone strikes on Russia crippled the world’s second-largest diesel supplier

paras.en: Ukraine launched massive drone assaults against Russia this week, hitting key oil infrastructure and signaling Kyiv intends to block the Kremlin from increasing diesel exports in defiance of President Donald Trump.
paras.zh: 乌克兰本周对俄罗斯发动大规模无人机袭击，袭击了关键的石油基础设施，并表明基辅打算无视唐纳德·特朗普总统，阻止克里姆林宫增加柴油出口。

paras.en: More than 1,000 Ukrainian drones targeted Russia on Sunday alone in one of the largest attacks this year, according to state media reports. The strikes set ablaze an oil export terminal in St. Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city and President Vladimir Putin's hometown.
paras.zh: 据官方媒体报道，仅周日就有 1000 多架乌克兰无人机瞄准了俄罗斯，这是今年最大规模的袭击之一。袭击导致俄罗斯第二大城市、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的家乡圣彼得堡的一个石油出口码头起火。

paras.en: Kyiv has ended its brief adherence to an energy ceasefire that Trump declared between Ukraine and Russia on Oct. 11. Moscow ignored that truce from the start and Kyiv vowed to retaliate.
paras.zh: 基辅结束了对特朗普于 10 月 11 日宣布的乌克兰和俄罗斯之间能源停火的短暂遵守。莫斯科从一开始就无视这一停火协议，基辅发誓要进行报复。

paras.en: Ukraine's drone strikes have achieved a scale, range and effectiveness that they have crippled Russia's diesel exports, said Tatiana Mitrova, an expert on the Russian oil industry at Columbia University's Center on Global Energy Policy. Before the attacks, Russia was the second-largest diesel supplier in the world after the U.S.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚大学全球能源政策中心俄罗斯石油工业专家塔蒂亚娜·米特罗娃表示，乌克兰的无人机袭击规模、范围和效力都严重削弱了俄罗斯的柴油出口。袭击发生前，俄罗斯是仅次于美国的全球第二大柴油供应国。

paras.en: As a result, Trump's deal with Putin to boost Russian diesel exports is likely dead in the water, said Matt Smith, director of commodity research at Kpler. "It seems unlikely that they'll be able to bring the volume of diesel back to the market that they are talking about without an energy ceasefire," Smith said.
paras.zh: Kpler 大宗商品研究主管马特·史密斯 (Matt Smith) 表示，因此，特朗普与普京促进俄罗斯柴油出口的协议可能会胎死腹中。史密斯说：“如果不实现能源停火，他们似乎不太可能将柴油数量带回他们正在谈论的市场。”

paras.en: Kyiv's strikes on Russian refineries and related oil infrastructure almost tripled to 31 in July compared with 11 in January, according to data from open-source intelligence firm Rochan Consulting in Warsaw, Poland.
paras.zh: 波兰华沙开源情报公司 Rochan Consulting 的数据显示，7 月份基辅对俄罗斯炼油厂和相关石油基础设施的袭击几乎增加了两倍，达到 31 起，而 1 月份有 11 起。

paras.en: The attacks slashed Russia's diesel exports by more than 75%, to 141,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September, compared with 608,000 bpd in the same period last year, according to Kpler data.
paras.zh: Kpler 数据显示，此次袭击导致俄罗斯 9 月份柴油出口量减少 75% 以上，至 141,000 桶/日，而去年同期为 608,000 桶/日。

paras.en: In response, Moscow banned exports in July to preserve domestic supplies. The Kremlin partially resumed shipments this month to fulfill the Trump-Putin deal.
paras.zh: 作为回应，莫斯科于 7 月禁止出口，以维持国内供应。克里姆林宫本月部分恢复了运输，以履行特朗普与普京的协议。

paras.en: Under Trump's diesel deal to relieve pressure on surging fuel prices, the Kremlin agreed to supply the global market with about 75,000 bpd in October and 124,000 bpd in November. But those export volumes are a rounding error compared with total demand, Mitrova said.
paras.zh: 根据特朗普为缓解燃油价格飙升压力而达成的柴油协议，克里姆林宫同意在 10 月份向全球市场供应约 75,000 桶/日，在 11 月份向全球市场供应约 124,000 桶/日。但米特罗娃表示，与总需求相比，这些出口量存在四舍五入误差。

paras.en: The Ukrainians are regularly launching swarms of drones now that number in the hundreds, compared with dozens earlier in the war, Mitrova said. They are also striking deeper into Russian territory, she said. In July, Kyiv hit Russia's largest refinery at Omsk, deep in Siberia near the Kazakhstan border, more than 1,000 miles from Ukraine.
paras.zh: 米特罗娃说，乌克兰定期发射无人机群，目前数量已达数百架，而战争初期只有数十架。她说，他们还深入俄罗斯领土。 7月，基辅袭击了位于鄂木斯克的俄罗斯最大炼油厂，该炼油厂位于西伯利亚深处，靠近哈萨克斯坦边境，距离乌克兰1000多英里。

paras.en: And they have learned to target more complex refinery equipment that is harder to repair, Mitrova said. A destroyed fuel tank takes just a couple of weeks to fix, she said. But replacing a secondary refining unit, for example, requires supply chains outside Russia, the analyst said.
paras.zh: 米特罗娃说，他们已经学会瞄准更复杂、更难维修的炼油设备。她说，被毁坏的油箱只需几周就能修复。但分析师表示，例如，更换二级炼油装置需要俄罗斯以外的供应链。

paras.en: "You cannot just order it on Alibaba," Mitrova said. "You need to make your order in advance and therefore securing this equipment quickly is not possible. You need to compensate for the risks of all the parties involved because [counterparties] are violating sanctions."
paras.zh: “你不能只在阿里巴巴上订购，”米特罗娃说。 “你需要提前下订单，因此不可能快速获得这些设备。你需要补偿所有相关方的风险，因为[交易对手]违反了制裁。”

paras.en: "You have to wait at least for several months if the right equipment is destroyed," she said.
paras.zh: “如果正确的设备被毁坏，你必须等待至少几个月，”她说。

paras.en: With midterm elections less than two weeks away, Trump has blamed Ukraine for surging diesel prices that are jeopardizing Republicans' election chances.
paras.zh: 距离中期选举还有不到两周的时间，特朗普指责乌克兰柴油价格飙升，危及共和党的选举机会。

paras.en: Nationally, diesel cost $6.32 per gallon on average Tuesday, nearly 75% above the same period last year, according to AAA.
paras.zh: 根据 AAA 的数据，周二全国柴油平均价格为每加仑 6.32 美元，比去年同期上涨近 75%。

paras.en: But the diesel market was already under pressure due to Trump's decision to go to war with Iran in late February. Tehran's attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes by its Houthi militant allies on oil infrastructure of U.S. Gulf Arab allies have disrupted fuel exports from the Middle East.
paras.zh: 但由于特朗普二月底决定与伊朗开战，柴油市场已经面临压力。德黑兰对霍尔木兹海峡油轮的袭击，以及胡塞武装盟友对美国海湾阿拉伯盟友石油基础设施的袭击，都扰乱了中东的燃料出口。

paras.en: Diesel exports through Hormuz, for example, are down about 540,000 bpd compared with last year, Kpler's Smith said. Global diesel exports have fallen about 1 million bpd due to lost supplies from Russia and the Middle East, he said.
paras.zh: Kpler 的 Smith 表示，例如，通过霍尔木兹的柴油出口量比去年减少了约 54 万桶/日。他表示，由于俄罗斯和中东的供应减少，全球柴油出口量减少了约 100 万桶/日。

paras.en: Trump's options to reduce fuel prices are limited. The underlying problem is the shortfall of refining capacity due to damage from two wars that don't appear close to ending soon. U.S. refiners are already working at maximum capacity to fill the gap as much as possible.
paras.zh: 特朗普降低燃油价格的选择有限。根本问题是由于两场似乎尚未结束的战争造成的损害而导致炼油能力不足。美国炼油厂已经在开足马力生产，以尽可能填补缺口。

paras.en: The International Energy Agency warned this month that diesel supplies will likely remain constrained well into 2027. "The diesel tightness is likely going to persist in the coming months and prices are going to remain elevated," Smith said.
paras.zh: 国际能源署本月警告称，柴油供应在 2027 年很可能仍将受到限制。史密斯表示，“未来几个月，柴油供应紧张的情况可能会持续，价格将保持高位。”

articles.title: New Mexico AG lawsuit accuses Epstein's attorney and accountant of facilitating sex trafficking

paras.en: New Mexico's attorney general on Wednesday filed a federal lawsuit accusing Jeffrey Epstein's long-time personal lawyer and accountant of facilitating Epstein's sex trafficking operation.
paras.zh: 新墨西哥州总检察长周三提起联邦诉讼，指控杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的长期私人律师和会计师为爱泼斯坦的性交易活动提供便利。

paras.en: The civil suit alleges that the attorney, Darren Indyke, and the accountant, Richard Kahn, helped finance and conceal Epstein's sex trafficking, which included the abuse of girls and young women at his Zorro Ranch in Santa Fe County, New Mexico.
paras.zh: 民事诉讼指控律师达伦·因代克和会计师理查德·卡恩帮助资助和隐瞒爱泼斯坦的性交易，其中包括在新墨西哥州圣达菲县的佐罗牧场虐待女孩和年轻女性。

paras.en: Indyke and Kahn are beneficiaries of Epstein's 1953 Trust, co-executors of Epstein's estate, and administrators of the revocable trust, whose name comes from the year of the convicted sex offender's birth.
paras.zh: 印代克和卡恩是爱泼斯坦 1953 年信托的受益人、爱泼斯坦遗产的共同执行人以及可撤销信托的管理人，该信托的名字来自被定罪的性犯罪者的出生年份。

paras.en: New Mexico's suit asks a judge to block Indyke and Kahn from receiving payments from the estate as the case proceeds in U.S. District Court in New Mexico.
paras.zh: 新墨西哥州的诉讼要求法官阻止因代克和卡恩从遗产中收取款项，案件正在新墨西哥州的美国地方法院审理。

paras.en: Attorney General Raul Torrez's office said that Epstein's estate is currently valued at more than $107 million, and the suit says Indyke and Kahn are eligible for bequests of $50 million and $25 million, subject to the availability of funds.
paras.zh: 总检察长劳尔·托雷斯办公室表示，爱泼斯坦的遗产目前价值超过 1.07 亿美元，诉讼称，印代克和卡恩有资格获得 5000 万美元和 2500 万美元的遗产，具体取决于资金的可用性。

paras.en: "Jeffrey Epstein did not operate alone, and his death does not end the pursuit of accountability for the people who helped make his crimes possible," Torrez said in a statement.
paras.zh: 托雷兹在一份声明中说：“杰弗里·爱泼斯坦并非单独行动，他的死亡并没有结束对那些帮助他犯罪的人追究责任。”

paras.en: "The allegations in this lawsuit describe a network of people and financial arrangements that helped sustain and conceal the abuse of vulnerable girls and young women, including here in New Mexico," Torrez said. "Those who allegedly enabled this exploitation should not be allowed to profit from it while survivors continue to live with its consequences."
paras.zh: 托雷兹说：“这起诉讼中的指控描述了一个人员网络和财务安排，帮助维持和掩盖了对弱势女孩和年轻女性的虐待，包括在新墨西哥州。” “那些据称促成这种剥削的人不应被允许从中获利，而幸存者则继续承受其后果。”

paras.en: The suit comes a month after The Wall Street Journal reported that the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York had opened an investigation into Indyke and Kahn.
paras.zh: 一个月前，《华尔街日报》报道称，纽约南区美国检察官办公室已对印代克和卡恩展开调查。

paras.en: Indyke and Kahn earlier this year testified in private to the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, which has been investigating Epstein and his connections to various individuals.
paras.zh: 印代克和卡恩今年早些时候向众议院监督和政府改革委员会私下作证，该委员会一直在调查爱泼斯坦及其与多个个人的关系。

paras.en: Daniel Weiner, an attorney for Epstein's estate, in March said, "Both Mr. Indyke and Mr. Kahn reject as categorically false the suggestion that they knowingly facilitated or assisted Mr. Epstein in his sexual abuse or trafficking of women, or that they were aware of that abuse while they provided professional services for him."
paras.zh: 爱泼斯坦的遗产律师丹尼尔·韦纳 (Daniel Weiner) 在 3 月份表示，“印代克先生和卡恩先生都否认这样的说法，认为他们故意协助或协助爱泼斯坦先生进行性虐待或贩卖妇女，或者他们在为他提供专业服务时意识到这种虐待行为。”

paras.en: CNBC has requested comment from Weiner on the new lawsuit.
paras.zh: CNBC 已要求韦纳对新诉讼发表评论。

paras.en: The lawsuit alleges that Indyke and Kahn personally profited from their relationship to Epstein, who killed himself in a federal jail in New York in August 2019, weeks after being arrested on child sex trafficking charges.
paras.zh: 该诉讼称，印代克和卡恩个人从他们与爱泼斯坦的关系中获利，爱泼斯坦于 2019 年 8 月在纽约联邦监狱自杀，几周后，他因儿童性贩运指控被捕。

paras.en: "Between 2011 and 2019, Indyke received more than $16 million from Epstein and related entities, and Kahn received more than $10 million," Kahn's office said in a statement.
paras.zh: 卡恩办公室在一份声明中表示：“2011年至2019年间，印代克从爱泼斯坦及相关实体那里收到了超过1600万美元，卡恩则收到了超过1000万美元。”

paras.en: Torrez, at a press conference Wednesday, said that his office is continuing a criminal investigation of Epstein's sex trafficking operation. No criminal charges have been filed in connection with that probe.
paras.zh: 托雷兹在周三的新闻发布会上表示，他的办公室正在继续对爱泼斯坦的性交易活动进行刑事调查。尚未提出与该调查有关的刑事指控。

paras.en: Epstein's estate in February agreed to pay out as much as $35 million to settle a class action lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Manhattan that accused Indyke and Kahn of aiding and abetting Epstein's sex trafficking.
paras.zh: 今年 2 月，爱泼斯坦的遗产管理委员会同意支付高达 3500 万美元，以了结美国曼哈顿地区法院提起的集体诉讼，该诉讼指控印代克和卡恩协助和教唆爱泼斯坦进行性交易。

paras.en: The proposed settlement does not include any admission of misconduct by Indyke or Kahn. The judge handling last month endorsed a proposal by the suit's plaintiff to notify potential class members to submit claims on the settlement by conducting a four-week-long social media campaign on Facebook and Instagram.
paras.zh: 拟议的和解协议不包括因代克或卡恩承认任何不当行为。上个月审理该诉讼的法官批准了原告的一项提议，即通过在 Facebook 和 Instagram 上开展为期四个星期的社交媒体活动，通知潜在的集体成员就和解提出索赔。

paras.en: This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.
paras.zh: 这是突发新闻。请刷新以获取更新。

articles.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty in New Mexico Cambridge Analytica case

paras.en: Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties by a New Mexico court on Wednesday as part of a data privacy case that stemmed from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal from nearly a decade ago.
paras.zh: 周三，新墨西哥州一家法院命令 Meta 支付 250 亿美元的罚款，作为该公司近十年前剑桥分析丑闻引发的数据隐私案件的一部分。

paras.en: The penalty, revealed in a court filing, comes after a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse found in September the social media giant liable for misleading state citizens about how it safeguards and collects user data and prevents harmful information from flourishing on its services.
paras.zh: 一份法庭文件中披露了这项处罚，此前圣达菲法院的陪审团去年 9 月发现，这家社交媒体巨头在如何保护和收集用户数据以及防止有害信息在其服务上泛滥方面误导州公民，负有责任。

paras.en: Although the jury concluded that Meta had over 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices act, with each transgression carrying a civil penalty as high as $5,000, a New Mexico judge was responsible for determining the ultimate fine. The Wednesday filing showed that the state was awarded $219.5 billion, but the penalty was ultimately reduced to $25 billion.
paras.zh: 尽管陪审团得出的结论是，Meta 有超过 4,300 万次违反该州不公平行为法的行为，每次违规行为将面临高达 5,000 美元的民事处罚，但新墨西哥州的法官仍负责确定最终罚款金额。周三提交的文件显示，该州获得了 2195 亿美元的赔偿，但罚款最终减少至 250 亿美元。

paras.en: "The extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership, the size of New Mexico audiences reached, and the clear intentional and systematic nature of Facebook's repeated misstatements established in the trial record support the highest level of penalty allowed by the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act - $5,000 per violation found by the jury," New Mexico district court judge Francis Joseph Mathew wrote in the filing.
paras.zh: 新墨西哥州地方法院法官弗朗西斯·约瑟夫·马修在文件中写道：“陪审团发现的故意违规行为数量之多、行为的持续时间和重复性、违规行为涉及的范围、Facebook高级领导层的参与、新墨西哥州受众的规模，以及审判记录中确定的Facebook一再错误陈述的明显故意和系统性，支持了新墨西哥州不公平行为法允许的最高处罚——陪审团发现的每次违规行为5,000美元。”

paras.en: CNBC has reached out to Meta for comment on the penalty order.
paras.zh: CNBC 已联系 Meta，请其对处罚令发表评论。

paras.en: Meta previously resolved various Cambridge Analytica-derived data privacy lawsuits across the nation as part of an overarching August settlement of nearly $17 billion with a coalition of state attorneys general in a separate federal case related to child safety and mental health. But because New Mexico was not part of the settlement, the state's data privacy case that arose from Meta's Cambridge Analytica scandal proceeded to trial in September.
paras.zh: Meta 此前在全国范围内解决了多起剑桥分析衍生的数据隐私诉讼，作为 8 月份与州总检察长联盟就一项涉及儿童安全和心理健康的单独联邦案件达成的近 170 亿美元总体和解协议的一部分。但由于新墨西哥州并未参与和解，该州因 Meta 剑桥分析丑闻引发的数据隐私案件于 9 月进入审判阶段。

paras.en: In 2022, the social media giant agreed to pay $725 million to settle a class action lawsuit that also sprang from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal that kicked off in 2018. That scandal rocked the Mark Zuckerberg-led company before its official name change to Meta, and focused on allegations that the political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica improperly accessed the information of 87 million users, raising questions about Facebook's data handling practices.
paras.zh: 2022 年，这家社交媒体巨头同意支付 7.25 亿美元来和解一项集体诉讼，该诉讼也源于该公司 2018 年爆发的 Cambridge Analytica 丑闻。该丑闻在马克·扎克伯格领导的公司正式更名为 Meta 之前震动了这家公司，并重点关注政治咨询公司 Cambridge Analytica 不当获取 8700 万用户信息的指控，引发了人们对 Facebook 数据处理做法的质疑。

paras.en: Former New Mexico state Attorney General Hector Balderas originally filed the state's Cambridge Analytica-related lawsuit in 2021, while current AG Raúl Torrez oversaw the related trial.
paras.zh: 前新墨西哥州总检察长 Hector Balderas 最初于 2021 年对该州提起了与 Cambridge Analytica 相关的诉讼，而现任总检察长 Raúl Torrez 则负责监督相关审判。

paras.en: Torrez also led his state's child-safety related trial against Meta that resulted in a March jury ruling that the social media company should pay $375 million for violating the state's unfair practices act. A New Mexico judge would later order Meta to pay $567 million into an abatement fund as part of a second phase of the case that determined the social media firm's actions created a public nuisance.
paras.zh: 托雷兹还领导了该州针对 Meta 的儿童安全相关审判，陪审团在 3 月份裁定，这家社交媒体公司应因违反该州的不公平行为法而支付 3.75 亿美元。新墨西哥州的一名法官随后命令 Meta 向减排基金支付 5.67 亿美元，作为案件第二阶段的一部分，该案件确定该社交媒体公司的行为造成了公众滋扰。

paras.en: Meta said it disagreed with that New Mexico ruling and planned to appeal.
paras.zh: Meta 表示不同意新墨西哥州的裁决并计划上诉。

articles.title: The provocative new theory that could explain aging and disease

paras.en: As diseases go, type 2 diabetes and epilepsy seem to have little in common. One is a metabolic disorder involving high blood glucose and failing insulin, the other a matter of neurons and electrical pulses. So it is odd that both often respond to fasting. Likewise, depression, obesity, Alzheimer’s, heart disease—all are wildly different diseases, yet all are influenced by diet. This shared vulnerability points to metabolism—the way we harvest energy from the food we eat and use it to power our cells.
paras.zh: 随着疾病的发展，2 型糖尿病和癫痫似乎没有什么共同点。一种是涉及高血糖和胰岛素失效的代谢紊乱，另一种是神经元和电脉冲的问题。因此，奇怪的是，两者都经常对禁食做出反应。同样，抑郁症、肥胖症、阿尔茨海默病、心脏病——都是截然不同的疾病，但都受到饮食的影响。这种共同的脆弱性指向新陈代谢——我们从所吃的食物中获取能量并用它来为我们的细胞提供能量的方式。

paras.en: One of the leading proponents of an energy-centric view of disease is Martin Picard, a biologist who directs the Mitochondrial Psychobiology Group at Columbia University. “Once we see ourselves as energetic processes,” he says, “many things make sense that didn’t make sense from a molecular perspective.”
paras.zh: 以能量为中心的疾病观的主要支持者之一是生物学家马丁·皮卡德 (Martin Picard)，他是哥伦比亚大学线粒体心理生物学小组的负责人。 “一旦我们将自己视为充满活力的过程，”他说，“许多从分子角度来看没有意义的事情就变得有意义了。”

paras.en: Picard and a growing number of colleagues are making the big claim that many chronic diseases we treat as separate failures of separate organs may share one deeper problem: cells struggling to extract and use energy from food. If they are right, a common weakness runs beneath diseases now parceled out among different specialties, and medicine might have spent a century drawing boundaries in the wrong places.
paras.zh: 皮卡德和越来越多的同事提出了一个重大论断，即我们将许多慢性疾病视为不同器官的单独衰竭，但它们可能都存在一个更深层次的问题：细胞难以从食物中提取和利用能量。如果他们是对的，那么现在在不同专业之间分配的疾病背后存在着一个共同的弱点，而医学可能花了一个世纪的时间在错误的地方划定了界限。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: At the heart of this argument lie mitochondria, the microscopic organelles that live in our cells and convert the energy stored in molecules of food into adenosine triphosphate, or ATP, the molecular power pack that drives virtually every reaction in the body, whether it’s moving, thinking or healing. We produce our body weight in ATP every day, and we burn just as much.
paras.zh: 这一论点的核心在于线粒体，它是生活在我们细胞中的微观细胞器，将食物分子中储存的能量转化为三磷酸腺苷（ATP），这是驱动体内几乎所有反应的分子动力组，无论是运动、思考还是治疗。我们每天都会产生相当于体重的 ATP，并且燃烧同样多的 ATP。

paras.en: Any meltdown in our mitochondria will lead to a shortage of ATP, leaving cells with less energy to do their jobs. Picard believes many states of poor health start there, and his once unusual research focus is now mainstream. “Everybody agrees that mitochondrial dysfunction is part of aging biology,” says Matt Kaeberlein, former director of the Healthy Aging and Longevity Research Institute at the University of Washington. “It’s one of the hallmarks of aging. And I think you can make a pretty reasoned argument that mitochondrial dysfunction can precede and potentially drive many of the other hallmarks of aging.”
paras.zh: 线粒体的任何崩溃都会导致 ATP 短缺，从而使细胞完成其工作的能量减少。皮卡德认为，许多健康状况不佳的情况都是从这里开始的，他曾经不寻常的研究重点现在已成为主流。 “每个人都同意线粒体功能障碍是衰老生物学的一部分，”华盛顿大学健康衰老与长寿研究所前所长马特·凯伯莱因 (Matt Kaeberlein) 说。 “这是衰老的标志之一。我认为你可以提出一个非常合理的论点，即线粒体功能障碍可能先于并可能导致许多其他衰老标志。”

paras.en: “Mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to the vast majority of common diseases.” —Matt Kaeberlein University of Washington
paras.zh: “线粒体功能障碍可能导致绝大多数常见疾病。” —马特·凯伯莱因华盛顿大学

paras.en: Certainly, Kaeberlein says, health is about more than mitochondria. “If you’re going to argue that everything starts with mitochondrial dysfunction, I think most people would push back against that.” But the idea doesn’t need to explain all of aging to be worth chasing. “Mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to the vast majority of common diseases,” he says. “Almost any disease you look at, you find a mitochondrial connection.”
paras.zh: Kaeberlein 说，当然，健康不仅仅关乎线粒体。 “如果你认为一切都始于线粒体功能障碍，我想大多数人都会反对这一点。”但这个想法并不需要解释所有的衰老才值得追求。 “线粒体功能障碍可能导致绝大多数常见疾病，”他说。 “几乎任何你观察到的疾病，你都会发现线粒体的联系。”

paras.en: That connection has gerontologists and biohackers alike racing to understand what makes mitochondria tick—and what we can do to keep them ticking as long as possible.
paras.zh: 这种联系让老年学家和生物黑客都竞相了解是什么让线粒体运转起来，以及我们可以做些什么来让它们尽可能长时间地运转。

paras.en: Although mitochondria’s central role in our existence is often overlooked, scientists have understood their importance since the 1960s, when British biochemist Peter Mitchell proposed a then radical explanation for how mitochondria capture energy—work that earned him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1978. The process, Mitchell showed, is fundamentally electrical. Electrons stripped from the atoms of our food are drawn toward atoms that will accept them. Among the elements biology has to work with, oxygen exerts the strongest pull.
paras.zh: 尽管线粒体在我们生存中的核心作用经常被忽视，但自 20 世纪 60 年代以来，科学家们就认识到了它们的重要性，当时英国生物化学家彼得·米切尔 (Peter Mitchell) 对线粒体如何捕获能量提出了当时激进的解释，这一工作为他赢得了 1978 年诺贝尔化学奖。米切尔表明，这个过程从根本上讲是电的。从食物原子中剥离的电子被吸引到接受它们的原子上。在生物学所涉及的元素中，氧气的拉力最强。

paras.en: Animals owe their existence to that attraction. We eat food, break it down into simpler molecules and send those to the mitochondria in our cells, which pry off electrons and let them flow through a string of molecules in their membranes known as the electron transport chain. At each step in this chain, a portion of the electrons’ energy is siphoned off to pump protons across a membrane—Mitchell’s great insight—and the pressure of those protons rushing back through a molecular turbine is what makes ATP. At the end of the chain, oxygen accepts the electrons and, together with protons, becomes water.
paras.zh: 动物的存在归功于这种吸引力。我们吃食物，将其分解成更简单的分子，并将这些分子发送到细胞中的线粒体，线粒体撬开电子，让它们流过细胞膜中的一串分子，即电子传输链。在这条链的每一步，一部分电子能量都会被抽走，以泵送质子穿过膜——米切尔的伟大见解——而这些质子通过分子涡轮冲回的压力就是产生 ATP 的原因。在链的末端，氧接受电子并与质子一起变成水。

paras.en: As many observers have noted, this flow of electrons through the body resembles the flow of electricity through the power grid. Power plants drive electricity through wires and into our homes, where our devices tap that energy to light our rooms and power our lives. The current has to meet the right amount of resistance in the right places. Too little, and the energy races past without doing any work, eventually damaging other components.
paras.zh: 正如许多观察家所指出的，电子在体内的流动类似于电流在电网中的流动。发电厂通过电线将电力输送到我们的家中，我们的设备利用这些能量来照亮我们的房间并为我们的生活提供动力。电流必须在正确的地方遇到正确的电阻。太少了，能量会在不做任何功的情况下快速流逝，最终损坏其他部件。

paras.en: Something similar happens in our mitochondria. Under ideal conditions, electrons are slowed in their passage through the electron transport chain just enough that their energy can be transferred. But if the mitochondrial circuits are impaired or if there are simply more electrons from food pouring into the system than the mitochondria can handle, the flow can get bogged down. Electrons can then leak out of the chain, bonding with oxygen in the wrong parts of the mitochondria to form highly reactive free radicals that attack and deform neighboring molecules. These reactive oxygen species, or ROS, can do real damage to mitochondria, cells and organs.
paras.zh: 我们的线粒体中也发生了类似的情况。在理想条件下，电子通过电子传输链的速度减慢，刚好足以传输它们的能量。但是，如果线粒体回路受损，或者来自食物的电子流入系统的数量超出了线粒体的处理能力，那么流动就会陷入困境。然后电子可以从链中泄漏出来，与线粒体错误部分的氧结合，形成高反应性自由基，攻击邻近的分子并使其变形。这些活性氧（ROS）会对线粒体、细胞和器官造成真正的损害。

paras.en: No matter how smoothly electrons flow through mitochondria, a certain amount of ROS is unavoidable in everyday life. The classic free-radical theory of aging, first proposed in the 1950s, held that aging itself resulted from the relentless buildup of ROS in our cells, decade after decade, and the wear and tear this caused. Now we know the body is quite capable of repairing manageable amounts of ROS, which at lower levels can even act as signals, telling a cell to get to work. Only when the oxidative stress gets out of hand do mitochondria get dinged up, but when they do, they move electrons less efficiently, which leads to even more ROS and more damage. The brownouts spread. Eventually cells lose capacity, and the body follows.
paras.zh: 无论电子如何顺利地流过线粒体，日常生活中都不可避免地会产生一定量的活性氧。经典的自由基衰老理论于 20 世纪 50 年代首次提出，认为衰老本身是细胞中活性氧 (ROS) 数十年不断积累以及由此造成的磨损的结果。现在我们知道，身体有能力修复可控制数量的活性氧，在较低水平时，活性氧甚至可以充当信号，告诉细胞开始工作。只有当氧化应激失控时，线粒体才会受损，但当它们受损时，它们移动电子的效率就会降低，从而导致更多的活性氧和更多的损伤。限电情况蔓延开来。最终，细胞丧失了能力，身体也随之丧失。

paras.en: Picard has written in this magazine about mitochondria’s role in health. In November 2025 he and Nirosha Murugan, a biophysicist at Wilfrid Laurier University in Ontario, codified this concept in the journal Cell Metabolism as the energy resistance principle. If a major cause of chronic disease is simply too many food-derived electrons frying the mitochondrial wires, then a major goal of medicine should be to reduce that overload. “The secret to longevity,” Picard says, “is to find ways to live at optimal energy resistance.”
paras.zh: 皮卡德在这本杂志上撰写了有关线粒体在健康中的作用的文章。 2025 年 11 月，他和安大略省 Wilfrid Laurier 大学的生物物理学家 Nirosha Murugan 在《细胞代谢》杂志上将这一概念编纂为能量抵抗原理。如果慢性疾病的主要原因只是过多的食物衍生电子烧毁了线粒体，那么医学的主要目标应该是减少这种超负荷。皮卡德说：“长寿的秘诀是找到以最佳能量抵抗力生活的方法。”

paras.en: These disruptions in cellular energy can have very different consequences throughout the body. “The specific pathology depends on where the mitochondrial dysfunction is happening,” Kaeberlein says. “If it’s in the muscle, you get muscular degeneration, myopathies, things like that. If it’s in the heart, you get different types of heart disease.” The brain is no exception. “You get things like Parkinson’s disease. Certainly mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to other types of dementia, including Alzheimer’s.” The Alzheimer’s link is strong enough that Paula Moreira, who is co-editor in chief of the Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease and specializes in brain mitochondria, has taken to calling the disease “diabetes of the brain.”
paras.zh: 这些细胞能量的破坏可能会对整个身体产生截然不同的后果。 “具体的病理学取决于线粒体功能障碍发生的位置，”Kaeberlein 说。 “如果它在肌肉中，你就会患上肌肉退化、肌病等。如果它在心脏里，你就会患上不同类型的心脏病。”大脑也不例外。 “你会患上帕金森氏症等疾病。当然，线粒体功能障碍会导致其他类型的痴呆症，包括阿尔茨海默氏症。”阿尔茨海默病与阿尔茨海默病的联系非常紧密，以至于《阿尔茨海默病杂志》联合主编、专门研究脑线粒体的保拉·莫雷拉(Paula Moreira)将这种疾病称为“大脑糖尿病”。

paras.en: The claim that mitochondrial dysfunction is a factor in mental health disorders as well as physical ones is surprising to many people. It’s less intuitive to picture energy supply affecting our mind as it does our muscles, but the brain is the most energy-hungry organ in the body. Neurons are closer to Formula One race cars than to family sedans, burning fuel at a furious rate and threatening to blow up at any moment. If any cells are going to betray signs of energetic stress, it’s them.
paras.zh: 线粒体功能障碍是精神健康障碍和身体健康障碍的一个因素的说法令许多人感到惊讶。能量供应对大脑的影响不像对肌肉的影响那样直观，但大脑是身体中最需要能量的器官。神经元更接近一级方程式赛车，而不是家用轿车，它们以惊人的速度燃烧燃料，并有随时爆炸的危险。如果说有哪个细胞会暴露出能量压力的迹象，那就是它们了。

paras.en: As mitochondrial dysfunction has become a familiar suspect in disease and aging, efforts to tinker with it now range from a cottage industry of supplements, such as coenzyme Q10, that promise happier, healthier mitochondria, to experimental interventions involving gold nanoparticles. That worries Jonathan Jarry, a science communicator at McGill University’s Office for Science and Society in Montreal. “My concern is that people start to believe that this has been successfully translated into the clinic when it hasn’t,” he says. “So it’s one thing to say, ‘Hey, here’s what we know about this thing that’s in our cells. It’s really cool. People are studying this.’ And it’s another to say, ‘Hey, we know the problems that this causes, and we know how to fix this, and we can sell you solutions.’”
paras.zh: 由于线粒体功能障碍已成为疾病和衰老的常见疑点，目前对其进行修补的努力范围广泛，从家庭手工业的补充剂（如承诺让线粒体更快乐、更健康的辅酶 Q10），到涉及金纳米粒子的实验干预措施。这让蒙特利尔麦吉尔大学科学与社会办公室的科学传播员乔纳森·贾里感到担忧。 “我担心的是，人们开始相信这已经成功地转化为临床，但事实并非如此，”他说。 “所以说，‘嘿，这是我们对细胞中这个东西的了解。这真的很酷。人们正在研究这个。’而说‘嘿，我们知道这会导致什么问题，我们知道如何解决这个问题，我们可以向你出售解决方案’是另一回事。”

paras.en: Kaeberlein agrees that the hacks have thus far disappointed. “None of the data so far looks all that compelling,” he says. Of all the supplements suspected to have mito-boosting powers, he says only one is convincing. “The one I would point to is creatine. There’s a clear mitochondrial connection, and the biology is very plausible. I think it’s a very good supplement. It works in the context of also doing exercise, but there’s emerging evidence on creatine and brain function, at least in situations like sleep deprivation or severe cognitive stress. You can buffer the ATP supply of the brain and muscle with creatine.”
paras.zh: Kaeberlein 同意，到目前为止，黑客行为令人失望。 “到目前为止，没有任何数据看起来那么令人信服，”他说。他说，在所有被怀疑具有增强线粒体功能的补充剂中，只有一种是令人信服的。 “我要提到的是肌酸。它与线粒体有明显的联系，而且生物学上也很合理。我认为这是一种非常好的补充剂。它在锻炼的情况下也有效，但有新的证据表明肌酸和大脑功能有关，至少在睡眠不足或严重认知压力等情况下是这样。你可以用肌酸缓冲大脑和肌肉的 ATP 供应。”

paras.en: For now the boring advice has better evidence than the hacks: sleep, exercise and diet.
paras.zh: 目前，无聊的建议比睡眠、锻炼和饮食等窍门有更好的证据。

paras.en: Sleep is extraordinarily important to mitochondrial health. That may be a big part of what drives our need for it. Neuroscientists at the University of Oxford have recently found direct links between oxidative stress in the brain and the need to sleep. As neurons fire furiously over the course of the day, ROS can accumulate. Specialized neurons track that buildup, and when a certain threshold is reached, they send a sleep signal to the brain at large. During sleep, neurons go quiet, ROS are cleared, and damaged mitochondria are repaired or recycled.
paras.zh: 睡眠对线粒体健康极其重要。这可能是推动我们对其需求的重要原因。牛津大学的神经科学家最近发现大脑氧化应激与睡眠需求之间存在直接联系。当神经元在一天中剧烈放电时，活性氧就会积聚。专门的神经元会跟踪这种积累，当达到某个阈值时，它们会向整个大脑发送睡眠信号。在睡眠期间，神经元变得安静，活性氧被清除，受损的线粒体得到修复或回收。

paras.en: Exercise also improves the capacity of mitochondria to process energy, in part by stress-testing the system. Any kind of workout is a temporary emergency for the cells involved. Energy demand might rise to 100 times resting levels, which pushes mitochondria and their support systems to the limit, producing a burst of ROS and other stress signals. During recovery, though, the body responds to this challenge so it will be better prepared for the next one, fixing damaged tissue and building more blood vessels and mitochondria. The payoff is a system that can handle more energy without straining the rest of the time. The leg muscles of a marathoner can have twice as many mitochondria per cell as those of a couch potato, spreading the energetic load across much more capacity.
paras.zh: 运动还可以提高线粒体处理能量的能力，部分是通过对系统进行压力测试来实现的。任何形式的锻炼对于相关细胞来说都是暂时的紧急情况。能量需求可能会上升到静息水平的 100 倍，这会将线粒体及其支持系统推向极限，产生大量 ROS 和其他应激信号。然而，在恢复过程中，身体会对这一挑战做出反应，以便为下一个挑战做好更好的准备，修复受损的组织并构建更多的血管和线粒体。回报是系统可以处理更多的能量，而不会在其余时间造成压力。马拉松运动员的腿部肌肉每个细胞中的线粒体数量是沙发土豆的两倍，从而将能量负荷分散到更多的容量上。

paras.en: The system also gets better at repair, which may turn out to be a more important part of healthy aging than we’ve realized. Exercise triggers a process known as autophagy, the cell’s salvage system for worn-out parts, including mitochondria. Damaged material gets dismantled; useful components go back into circulation.
paras.zh: 该系统的修复能力也变得更好，这可能是健康衰老的一个比我们意识到的更重要的部分。运动会触发一种称为自噬的过程，这是细胞对磨损部件（包括线粒体）的抢救系统。损坏的材料被拆除；有用的成分重新回到循环中。

paras.en: Recycling also seems to help explain another old standby: calorie restriction. “Autophagy is an adaptive response to nutrient deprivation,” Kaeberlein says. “When you’re in nutrient shortage, you don’t have the energy to produce a bunch of new complex machinery, so you break down the damaged machinery, and then you can reuse those components. And the most important time to recycle is when you don’t have sufficient nutrients to build new machinery.”
paras.zh: Recycling also seems to help explain another old standby: calorie restriction. “Autophagy is an adaptive response to nutrient deprivation,” Kaeberlein says. “当你营养短缺时，你没有能量来生产一堆新的复杂机械，所以你需要分解损坏的机械，然后你可以重复使用这些部件。而回收最重要的时机是当你没有足够的营养来建造新机械时。”

paras.en: These disruptions in cellular energy can cause very different consequences throughout the body.
paras.zh: 细胞能量的这些破坏可能会导致整个身体产生非常不同的后果。

paras.en: That efficient scavenging can also clear damaged components before they become a liability. At the same time, reducing the amount of energy entering the system eases the load on mitochondria and reduces oxidative stress. Calorie reduction reliably improves health and lifespan in many organisms, including yeast, worms, flies and rodents. In primates, the results aren’t as clear, although long-running studies point to health benefits.
paras.zh: 这种有效的清除还可以在损坏的部件成为负担之前将其清除。同时，减少进入系统的能量可以减轻线粒体的负荷并减少氧化应激。热量减少确实可以改善许多生物体的健康和寿命，包括酵母、蠕虫、苍蝇和啮齿动物。在灵长类动物中，结果并不那么明确，尽管长期研究表明它对健康有益。

paras.en: Diet-based interventions have shown promise for the brain as well as the body, a connection physicians made long ago when they noted that fasting could often prevent seizures in people with epilepsy. “Hippocrates knew about it 2,000 years ago,” says Christopher Palmer, a Harvard Medical School psychiatrist and author of the 2022 book Brain Energy. “In the 1920s physicians put it to the test. And to their shock, it actually worked.”
paras.zh: 基于饮食的干预措施对大脑和身体都有好处，医生很早以前就注意到禁食通常可以预防癫痫患者的癫痫发作，从而建立了这种联系。 “希波克拉底在 2000 年前就知道了这一点，”哈佛医学院精神病学家、2022 年出版的《大脑能量》一书的作者克里斯托弗·帕尔默 (Christopher Palmer) 说道。 “20 世纪 20 年代，医生对其进行了测试。令他们震惊的是，它确实有效。”

paras.en: We now know a lot about the mechanisms of action, Palmer says, including “changes in neurotransmitter function, changes in hormone signaling, changes in epigenetics, reduced brain inflammation and changes in mitochondrial function.” Those changes seem to be linked to metabolic shifts, among them reductions in the load of glucose, the body’s standard fuel, which is produced mostly from carbohydrates. A ketogenic diet can reproduce fasting’s metabolic effects by strictly limiting carbohydrates and relying more on fat. When carb intake falls sharply, the liver turns fat into ketones, an alternative fuel for the brain and other tissues that may cause less metabolic stress. Whether this broader metabolic shift can improve psychiatric symptoms is now being put to the test.
paras.zh: 帕尔默说，我们现在对作用机制了解很多，包括“神经递质功能的变化、激素信号的变化、表观遗传学的变化、大脑炎症的减少和线粒体功能的变化。”这些变化似乎与代谢变化有关，其中包括葡萄糖负荷的减少，葡萄糖是人体的标准燃料，主要由碳水化合物产生。生酮饮食可以通过严格限制碳水化合物并更多地依赖脂肪来重现禁食的代谢效应。当碳水化合物摄入量急剧下降时，肝脏会将脂肪转化为酮，酮是大脑和其他组织的替代燃料，可能会减少代谢压力。这种更广泛的代谢转变是否可以改善精神症状现在正在接受考验。

paras.en: In July a team led by researchers at the San Francisco VA Medical Center published the first randomized controlled trial of a ketogenic diet in people with bipolar I disorder and schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. After a month, the ketogenic group showed clear metabolic improvements; the more striking psychiatric and cognitive gains turned up at four months—by which point the diet had been offered to everyone, eliminating the control-group comparison. The clinical signal remains intriguing but preliminary.
paras.zh: 7月，由旧金山退伍军人医疗中心的研究人员领导的团队发表了第一个针对I型双相情感障碍和精神分裂症谱系障碍患者的生酮饮食随机对照试验。一个月后，生酮组的代谢明显改善；更显着的精神和认知收益在四个月时出现——此时饮食已经提供给每个人，消除了对照组的比较。临床信号仍然令人感兴趣，但仍处于初步阶段。

paras.en: “We’ve known for decades that a ketogenic diet is effective for antiseizure,” Kaeberlein says. “It definitely has effects on brain metabolism that are potent. That’s going to affect mitochondrial dysfunction. So it’s reasonable to think a ketogenic diet will have broader-reaching effects on brain biology that could affect emotion, psychological state, cognitive abilities, all of those things.”
paras.zh: “几十年来我们就知道生酮饮食对于抗癫痫有效，”Kaeberlein 说。 “它肯定会对大脑新陈代谢产生强大的影响。这将影响线粒体功能障碍。因此，有理由认为生酮饮食将对大脑生物学产生更广泛的影响，可能影响情绪、心理状态、认知能力，所有这些。”

paras.en: Kaeberlein cautions that it is too early to assume that we understand how these incredibly complex systems work. “The arrows all point in the direction that repairing and preserving mitochondrial function during aging is important for the lifespan and health span benefits we see from these interventions. But because all of these things are multifactorial, it’s hard to know how much is because of their effects on mitochondria versus other things that these interventions are doing.” The wrinkle is that mitochondria live inside the cell and depend on it, so anything that improves their function will improve the cell, but anything that improves the cell will also improve them.
paras.zh: Kaeberlein 警告说，现在假设我们了解这些极其复杂的系统如何工作还为时过早。 “所有箭头都指向，在衰老过程中修复和保护线粒体功能对于我们从这些干预措施中看到的寿命和健康益处非常重要。但由于所有这些事情都是多因素的，所以很难知道有多少是因为它们对线粒体的影响与这些干预措施正在做的其他事情有关。”问题是线粒体生活在细胞内并依赖于细胞，所以任何改善线粒体功能的东西都会改善细胞，但任何改善细胞的东西也会改善它们。

paras.en: On their face, none of these interventions are revolutionary. The appeal of the energy-centric perspective is that it gives familiar advice—eat lightly, sleep well, get exercise—a common language. “The disease-centric point of view looks at a singular snapshot and then looks backward to see how that applies to health. The energy-resistance framework flips that,” Murugan says. “It reframes health as a dynamic process, and it allows us to look at how different interventions can influence that process. It puts them into context.”
paras.zh: 从表面上看，这些干预措施都不是革命性的。以能量为中心的观点的吸引力在于，它提供了熟悉的建议——清淡饮食、睡好觉、锻炼身体——这是一种共同语言。 “以疾病为中心的观点着眼于单一的快照，然后回顾它如何应用于健康。能量抵抗框​​架翻转了这一点，”穆鲁根说。 “它将健康重新定义为一个动态过程，使我们能够了解不同的干预措施如何影响该过程。它将它们置于背景之中。”

paras.en: A good example is type 2 diabetes. “From a molecular perspective,” Picard says, “diabetes is excess blood sugar and insulin resistance. So you fix it with drugs. You give insulin to override the resistance.” He reads insulin resistance differently. In some cases, he argues, cells may begin to resist glucose because their mitochondria are already struggling to process the fuel coming in. In that telling, they need a break, Picard says, not an override.
paras.zh: 2 型糖尿病就是一个很好的例子。 “从分子角度来看，”皮卡德说，“糖尿病是血糖过高和胰岛素抵抗。所以你可以用药物来解决它。你可以注射胰岛素来克服抵抗力。”他对胰岛素抵抗的解读不同。他认为，在某些情况下，细胞可能会开始抵抗葡萄糖，因为它们的线粒体已经在努力处理进入的燃料。皮卡德说，在这种情况下，它们需要休息，而不是超控。

paras.en: An energy-centric perspective may also offer early warning signs. Cells under stress release a signaling protein known as GDF15. “It’s the way cells tell other cells, ‘I’m not doing well,’” Picard says. High levels of GDF15, which also rise in pregnancy and illness, trigger feelings of malaise and nausea—a built-in brake on energetically costly activities such as movement and digestion. He thinks the body is then able to conserve energy while confronting the internal challenges. High levels are also among the best predictors of future disease and mortality, which he takes as strong evidence that energetic dysfunction within cells precedes later problems—and may offer us an early opportunity to head them off.
paras.zh: 以能源为中心的观点也可能提供早期预警信号。处于压力下的细胞会释放一种称为 GDF15 的信号蛋白。 “这是细胞告诉其他细胞‘我做得不好’的方式，”皮卡德说。高水平的 GDF15（在怀孕和生病时也会升高）会引发不适和恶心的感觉，这是对运动和消化等耗能活动的内在阻碍。他认为身体能够在应对内部挑战的同时保存能量。高水平也是未来疾病和死亡率的最佳预测因素之一，他认为这是强有力的证据，表明细胞内的能量功能障碍先于后来的问题，并且可能为我们提供早期阻止它们的机会。

paras.en: But beyond such practical applications, the biggest appeal of seeing health through the lens of energy may be the new light it shines on the very concept of disease. “Once we see ourselves energetically, it’s going to change how we teach and practice medicine,” Picard says. Rather than fixing parts piecemeal after they break down, we can ask what keeps us all happily humming along in the first place. In a sense, we are all energy benders, channeling an endless flow of what was once sunlight through the labyrinth of our molecules and gracefully shaping it into this thing we call life.
paras.zh: 但除了这些实际应用之外，通过能量透镜看待健康的最大吸引力可能在于它为疾病概念带来了新的启发。 “一旦我们充满活力地看待自己，它将改变我们的医学教学和实践方式，”皮卡德说。我们不应该在零件损坏后将其零碎地修复，而应该问是什么让我们所有人都能快乐地继续前进。从某种意义上说，我们都是能量扭曲者，将曾经的阳光源源不断地引导穿过我们分子的迷宫，并将其优雅地塑造成我们称之为生命的东西。

articles.title: Republican congressional candidate Tom Stalcup on how both parties abuse science for political gain

paras.en: Tom Stalcup, the Republican Party’s candidate to represent Massachusetts’s fourth district in Congress, does not like the way American politicians talk about science.
paras.zh: 代表马萨诸塞州第四选区的共和党国会候选人汤姆·斯塔尔卡普(Tom Stalcup)不喜欢美国政客谈论科学的方式。

paras.en: Stalcup, who holds a Ph.D. in physics from Florida State University, faces an uphill challenge to defeat incumbent Democrat Jake Auchincloss, who was elected in 2020. The district has not been represented by a Republican since 1947.
paras.zh: Stalcup，拥有博士学位。佛罗里达州立大学物理学博士面临着击败 2020 年当选的现任民主党人杰克·奥金克洛斯 (Jake Auchincloss) 的艰巨挑战。自 1947 年以来，该选区就没有共和党代表。

paras.en: That long-shot status seems to have offered Stalcup a little more freedom—he’s distanced himself from the party’s standard line on issues such as climate change and drug pricing. But that doesn’t mean he believes the Democrats are any better when it comes to science-related policies.
paras.zh: 这种可能性不大的地位似乎给斯塔尔卡普提供了更多的自由——他在气候变化和药品定价等问题上与党的标准路线保持了距离。但这并不意味着他认为民主党在科学相关政策方面做得更好。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In an interview with Scientific American, Stalcup explains how he hopes to apply the scientific method to making policy, what years of misinformation have done to the American public and why he believes both parties abuse science for political gain.
paras.zh: 在接受《科学美国人》采访时，斯塔尔卡普解释了他希望如何应用科学方法来制定政策、多年来的错误信息对美国公众造成了什么影响，以及为什么他认为两党滥用科学来获取政治利益。

paras.en: [An edited transcript of the interview follows.]
paras.zh: [编辑后的采访记录如下。]

paras.en: You are a scientist by training. Can you tell us about your field of expertise?
paras.zh: 你是一位受过训练的科学家。您能告诉我们您的专业领域吗？

paras.en: I have a Ph.D. in condensed matter physics. I got my degree while working at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory in Tallahassee, [Fla.], where we studied organic superconductors, which are two-dimensional period materials—crystals actually—that become superconductors at various temperatures. I was studying copper bromine, and it had an interesting transition around 80 kelvins. I published results that showed that the superconducting transition temperature, as well as the effective mass of the electron and other properties of the material, would actually be changed based on how slowly or fast you cool it.
paras.zh: 我有博士学位。在凝聚态物理中。我在佛罗里达州塔拉哈西的国家高磁场实验室工作时获得了学位，在那里我们研究有机超导体，这是一种二维周期材料（实际上是晶体），在不同温度下会变成超导体。我正在研究溴铜，它在 80 开尔文左右有一个有趣的转变。我发表的结果表明，超导转变温度以及电子的有效质量和材料的其他特性实际上会根据冷却速度的慢慢或快慢而改变。

paras.en: After you received your Ph.D., you founded a company, Upward Innovations. How do you use your scientific background there? Why didn’t you go into academia?
paras.zh: 获得博士学位后，您创立了一家公司，Upward Innovations。你在那里如何利用你的科学背景？你为什么不进入学术界？

paras.en: That’s a company that I founded in 2004. I graduated [with] my Ph.D. in 2000. I did not go into academia. I was pretty burned out after getting my Ph.D.; it was a pretty grueling experience. So I got a job at an electronics firm where they were building a remote weather station, and so I made a spin-off company that allowed their data to basically get on the cloud.
paras.zh: 那是我于 2004 年创立的一家公司。我获得了博士学位。 2000年，我没有进入学术界。获得博士学位后，我感到非常疲惫。这是一次非常痛苦的经历。所以我在一家电子公司找到了一份工作，他们在那里建造一个远程气象站，所以我成立了一家分拆公司，让他们的数据基本上可以上传到云端。

paras.en: As a company, we do business as DataGarrison.com. That’s the website where users can get their data. Our remote weather stations are situated all around the world, and their data is purchased by researchers studying climate change. We don’t really take a position on what they’re going to measure. We just provide the equipment to allow them to measure. And of course, I’m not avoiding the climate change issue because I completely agree—even as a Republican—that climate change is real and human-caused. We have the data to prove it. It’s not an item of debate. So that’s where it differentiates me as a Republican.
paras.zh: 作为一家公司，我们以 DataGarrison.com 名义开展业务。这是用户可以获取数据的网站。我们的远程气象站遍布世界各地，其数据由研究气候变化的研究人员购买。我们并没有真正对他们要衡量的内容采取立场。我们只是提供设备让他们进行测量。当然，我并不是回避气候变化问题，因为我完全同意——即使作为一名共和党人——气候变化是真实存在的，而且是人为造成的。我们有数据证明这一点。这不是一个值得争论的话题。这就是我作为共和党人的不同之处。

paras.en: It’s fun, interesting work. We have a bunch [of stations] in Antarctica. And recently, in the past five or 10 years, we added cameras to the systems. [Our stations] are actually studying sea ice down in Antarctica now and how it moves. The Fish and Wildlife Service uses them to study birds in one of the most remote islands on Earth, called Jarvis Island, in the middle Pacific.
paras.zh: 这是有趣、有趣的工作。我们在南极洲有很多[站]。最近，在过去的五年或十年里，我们在系统中添加了摄像头。 [我们的站]实际上正在研究南极洲的海冰及其移动方式。鱼类和野生动物管理局利用它们来研究地球上最偏远的岛屿之一贾维斯岛（位于太平洋中部）的鸟类。

paras.en: On your website, you say you put science and reason ahead of partisan politics. Can you explain how your scientific background affects your approach to policy?
paras.zh: 在您的网站上，您说您将科学和理性置于党派政治之上。您能解释一下您的科学背景如何影响您的政策方针吗？

paras.en: Science informs all of it. Science is often used when it’s convenient for either side, and that’s just wrong, and both sides do it—Republicans and Democrats. If the science doesn’t agree with what they say, they just ignore it, and it’s troublesome. Science cuts both ways, and that’s why I say, “Science over politics.”
paras.zh: 科学告诉了这一切。科学常常在对任何一方都方便的时候被使用，但这是错误的，共和党和民主党双方都这样做。如果科学不同意他们所说的，他们就会忽略它，这很麻烦。科学是双向的，这就是为什么我说“科学高于政治”。

paras.en: Throughout my life, I saw a deterioration in the U.S. media, where we were just given misinformation. Science is the search for truth and the search for facts that back up what [argument] you’re trying to present. One of the biggest examples that really affected me was George W. Bush’s invasion of Iraq based on lies. Back in the day, seven in 10 Americans believed that Saddam Hussein was involved in the 9/11 attacks.
paras.zh: 在我的一生中，我看到美国媒体的恶化，我们只得到错误的信息。科学是对真理的探索，是对支持你试图提出的[论点]的事实的探索。真正影响我的最大例子之一是乔治·W·布什基于谎言入侵伊拉克。当时，十分之七的美国人认为萨达姆·侯赛因参与了 9/11 袭击。

paras.en: It’s not just the Iraq War; it’s every subject. You can make an argument for anything by selecting and cherry-picking facts and omitting facts and sound convincing. There are basically two media bubbles now, where each side of the country is being misled about the other side—not through lies per se but by selectively, carefully curated facts and omissions of other facts. I’m trying to cut through that.
paras.zh: 这不仅仅是伊拉克战争；这是每个主题。你可以通过选择和挑选事实、省略事实来为任何事情提出论据，并且听起来令人信服。现在基本上存在两个媒体泡沫，国家的每一方都被对方误导——不是通过谎言本身，而是通过有选择地、精心策划的事实和对其他事实的遗漏。我正在努力解决这个问题。

paras.en: You talk a lot about using data-driven solutions to reduce health care costs. How would you go about doing that?
paras.zh: 您多次谈到使用数据驱动的解决方案来降低医疗保健成本。你会怎样做呢？

paras.en: One solution is to have broad price negotiations. The data show that there is active legal corruption going on. Health insurance agencies, as well as the pharmaceutical companies, keep prices high, and they call it capitalism. I’m all for capitalism. But when it comes to a life-or-death decision, there’s a huge demand for staying alive, and you shouldn’t use someone’s life-or-death decision to price gouge them. My aunt died recently of cancer, in the last few months of her life she was spending $10,000 a month on prescription medications, and that’s just atrocious and should be illegal.
paras.zh: 一种解决方案是进行广泛的价格谈判。数据显示，法律腐败现象十分活跃。健康保险机构以及制药公司将价格维持在高位，他们称之为资本主义。我完全支持资本主义。但当涉及到生死攸关的决定时，人们对生存的需求很大，你不应该利用某人的生死攸关的决定来哄抬他们的价格。我的阿姨最近死于癌症，在她生命的最后几个月里，她每月花费 10,000 美元购买处方药，这太残忍了，应该是非法的。

paras.en: I’m a Republican saying that, in some areas, socialism is required. We do it for the national defense of the country. There’s no reason why we can’t socialize the defense of the human body and keep it safe and protected from outside pathogens.
paras.zh: 我是一名共和党人，他说，在某些领域，社会主义是必要的。我们这样做是为了国家的国防。我们没有理由不能社会化人体的防御并保证其安全并免受外界病原体的侵害。

paras.en: To fight this terrible plague of corruption that’s driving these high costs, you need a lot of money. Let’s say you solve the health care [problem]—the next election cycle, these people that were making money on it will then give a lot of money again to reverse what you did. And so I think Republicans must agree to eliminate Citizens United and reform campaign finance. [Editor’s Note: Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission is a 2010 Supreme Court ruling that lifted campaign spending restrictions on corporations and other outside groups.]
paras.zh: 为了对抗导致高昂成本的可怕腐败瘟疫，您需要大量资金。假设你解决了医疗保健[问题]——下一个选举周期，那些靠它赚钱的人会再次捐出很多钱来扭转你所做的事情。因此，我认为共和党人必须同意取消公民联合组织并改革竞选财务。 [编者注：公民联合诉联邦选举委员会是最高法院 2010 年的一项裁决，取消了对企业和其他外部团体的竞选支出限制。]

paras.en: You acknowledge that climate change is real and measurable. How would you make your voice heard within your party, given that the most senior Republican leaders, including the president, have called it a hoax?
paras.zh: 您承认气候变化是真实且可衡量的。鉴于包括总统在内的最高级共和党领导人都称这是一场骗局，您将如何在党内表达您的声音？

paras.en: It’s not a hoax. It’s real. However, you can point to certain instances where companies have used their clout and connections to make a lot of money off the climate change crisis. I think [former president Barack] Obama got in a bit of trouble for giving a lot of money Solyndra, a company that failed quickly after they received many millions of dollars.
paras.zh: 这不是骗局。这是真的。然而，你可以举出一些例子，在这些例子中，公司利用自己的影响力和关系从气候变化危机中赚了很多钱。我认为（前总统巴拉克）奥巴马因为向 Solyndra 提供了大量资金而陷入了一些麻烦，这家公司在收到数百万美元后很快就倒闭了。

paras.en: I think there are two things. I think some people say [they don’t believe in climate change] just because they want to get votes, and I think some people actually believe that because they’re in this media bubble. I’ve done a lot of work as a pro se litigant in the courts in the past 10 or 20 years, and there’s something called Rule 11, where you’re not allowed to omit facts when you’re presenting information to the court. I think the same thing should apply to journalists. If there is a channel or people providing news to the country, the court of public opinion should not be able to be swayed by the omission of facts or [by] misleading facts.
paras.zh: 我认为有两件事。我认为有些人说[他们不相信气候变化]只是因为他们想获得选票，而且我认为有些人实际上相信这一点，因为他们处于这个媒体泡沫中。在过去的 10 或 20 年里，我作为自诉当事人在法庭上做了很多工作，有一条叫做“第 11 条”的规则，即当你向法庭提供信息时，不得遗漏事实。我认为同样的事情也应该适用于记者。如果有渠道或人向国家提供新闻，舆论法庭就不能因为遗漏事实或误导事实而动摇。

paras.en: Congress recently paused a Trump administration effort to charge political appointees with deciding scientific grant funding. Do you support the administration’s plan?
paras.zh: 国会最近暂停了特朗普政府要求政治任命者决定科学拨款的努力。你支持政府的计划吗？

paras.en: I would put a moratorium on all of Trump’s changes regarding the [National Science Foundation] and the [Department of Health and Human Services]. He’s taking the sledgehammer to a problem rather than a scalpel. There’s obviously some favoritism going on in the NSF; there is some politics going on, which I disagree with. I disagreed with it even back when I was a grad student. Everyone knows that there’s politics involved in grants sometimes, and that should be excised from the grant-making procedures. But taking the sledgehammer to this problem, as Trump has done, is the wrong approach. There are so many people affected, in my district, by his approach, and it’s not good for the country. Yes, there are abuses, just like there were in other almost every area of government, and they must be tackled surgically, not with a sledgehammer.
paras.zh: 我将暂停特朗普对[国家科学基金会]和[卫生与公众服务部]的所有改变。他用大锤而不是手术刀来解决问题。 NSF 中显然存在一些偏袒行为；有一些政治因素正在发生，我不同意。甚至在我还是研究生的时候我也不同意这一点。每个人都知道，资助有时会涉及政治，这应该从资助程序中剔除。但像特朗普那样用大锤来解决这个问题是错误的做法。在我的地区，有很多人受到他的做法的影响，这对国家不利。是的，确实存在滥用职权的情况，就像政府其他几乎每个领域都存在滥用职权一样，必须通过外科手术来解决这些问题，而不是用大锤来解决。

paras.en: [The U.S. was] and always has been a leader in technology and advancements in science: the telephone, the Internet, the light bulb. I don’t think Trump understands basic scientific research. There’s no real immediate turnaround and investment in basic research. That’s the research I was doing. No one made money off increasing the superconducting transition temperature by two or three kelvins, but it was important to understand the broader science surrounding superconductivity in general. [That could] revolutionize all electronics, but again, it’s not immediate, and if we don’t fund it anymore, we’re going to fall behind. And I don’t think Trump wants that. I just don’t think he sees it clearly enough to make proper decisions.
paras.zh: [美国]过去并且一直是技术和科学进步的领导者：电话、互联网、灯泡。我认为特朗普不懂基础科学研究。基础研究并没有真正的立即转变和投资。这就是我正在做的研究。没有人通过将超导转变温度提高两到三个开尔文来赚钱，但了解围绕超导性的更广泛的科学是很重要的。 [这可能]彻底改变所有电子产品，但同样，这不是立竿见影的，如果我们不再资助它，我们就会落后。我认为特朗普不希望这样。我只是认为他看得不够清楚，无法做出正确的决定。

paras.en: Almost all the other candidates running in the midterms who have science backgrounds are running as Democrats. Do you think that the Republican Party has a science problem?
paras.zh: 几乎所有参加中期选举的具有科学背景的候选人都是民主党人。你认为共和党有科学问题吗？

paras.en: I do, but I believe the Democrats have a science problem as well. There are many issues on which Democrats will not side with science. What the Democrats do with science, they also do with minorities. They co-opt a movement and take it as their own, and that’s just not the proper thing to do. If you’re going to use science, you have to let it cut both ways. And if science doesn’t really support what you’re saying, then you can’t claim to be the party of science.
paras.zh: 我愿意，但我相信民主党也有科学问题。在许多问题上，民主党人不会站在科学一边。民主党对科学所做的事情，他们也对少数族裔所做的事情。他们选择一项运动并将其视为自己的运动，但这不是正确的做法。如果你要运用科学，你就必须让它发挥双向作用。如果科学并不真正支持你所说的，那么你就不能声称自己是科学党。

paras.en: [During the pandemic], it seemed pretty obvious to a lot of people that COVID most likely came from a laboratory in China. And all of the power centers of the Left fought tooth and nail against that narrative and called the people who would say that conspiracy theorists. [Editor’s Note: According to a 2025 World Health Organization report, the lab leak possibility “cannot be confirmed nor eliminated” because of a lack of evidence.]
paras.zh: [在大流行期间]，对很多人来说，很明显，新冠病毒很可能来自中国的一个实验室。所有左派权力中心都竭尽全力反对这种说法，并称那些会说这种说法的人是阴谋论者。 [编者注：根据世界卫生组织2025年的报告，由于缺乏证据，实验室泄漏的可能性“无法确认或消除”。]

paras.en: It’s a tribalism thing to say we’re with science—and it’s not necessarily science; it’s virtue signaling.
paras.zh: 说我们支持科学是一种部落主义，但它不一定是科学；这是美德信号。

paras.en: Some of my really good friends are also Ph.D.s in physics; many of them are Democrats. And they believe that half the country is stupid—not just wrong but actually dumb. I think it comforts people to feel like they’re better and superior, and that makes the Right feel very upset that people are viewing them in that way. It creates a lot of friction, and it’s just not good for the country.
paras.zh: 我的一些真正的好朋友也是物理学博士。其中许多人是民主党人。他们认为一半的国家都是愚蠢的——不仅是错误的，而且实际上是愚蠢的。我认为这会让人们感到自己更好、更优越，这会让右派感到非常不安，因为人们以这种方式看待他们。它会造成很多摩擦，而且对国家不利。

articles.title: A Wall Is Also a Road explores alien consciousness, slime mold life-forms and Pompeii

paras.en: Rachel Feltman: For Scientific American’s Science Quickly, I’m Rachel Feltman. Today we’re taking a break from science fact to talk about some recent science fiction. My guest is journalist, editor and author Annalee Newitz. You may know some of their nonfiction titles like Four Lost Cities: A Secret History of the Urban Age, Stories Are Weapons: Psychological Warfare and the American Mind and Scatter, Adapt, and Remember: How Humans Will Survive a Mass Extinction. But their journalistic research on science and technology has also fueled popular fiction titles like The Future of Another Timeline and, one of my personal favorites, Automatic Noodle. It takes place in a post-war San Franscisco and features a bunch of robots starting their own noodle restaurant. It’s really wonderful, you should check it out.
paras.zh: 雷切尔·费尔特曼：《科学美国人》的《科学快报》，我是雷切尔·费尔特曼。今天我们暂时抛开科学事实，来谈谈最近的一些科幻小说。我的嘉宾是记者、编辑兼作家安娜莉·纽维茨。您可能知道他们的一些非小说类书籍，例如《四个失落的城市：城市时代的秘密历史》、《故事是武器：心理战和美国思想》和《分散、适应和记住：人类如何在大规模灭绝中生存》。但他们对科学技术的新闻研究也推动了流行小说的发展，比如《另一个时间线的未来》，以及我个人最喜欢的作品之一《自动面条》。故事发生在战后的旧金山，一群机器人创办了自己的面馆。真的很精彩，你应该看看。

paras.en: Anyway, Annalee is here today to talk about their latest book, A Wall Is Also a Road. It’s a genre-bending odyssey featuring sentient slime molds, ancient Roman sex workers and extraterrestrial academics who prove that, no matter how alien your physiology may be, the stress of working on a dissertation is completely universal.
paras.zh: 无论如何，Annalee 今天在这里谈论他们的最新书《墙也是路》。这是一部跨流派的冒险之旅，讲述了有感知力的粘菌、古罗马性工作者和外星学者的故事，他们证明，无论你的生理机能多么陌生，写论文的压力是完全普遍的。

paras.en: Annalee, thanks so much for coming on to chat with us today
paras.zh: Annalee，非常感谢您今天接受我们的采访

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Annalee Newitz: Yeah, thanks for having me.
paras.zh: 安娜莉·纽维茨：是的，谢谢你邀请我。

paras.en: Feltman: So I wanna talk about your latest book. I’m really, really enjoying it. I think it pulls a lot from your background as a science writer who’s written a lot of nonfiction. So I would love to just start with how this idea first started.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：所以我想谈谈你的最新书。我真的非常非常享受它。我认为这与你作为一名写过很多非小说类作品的科普作家的背景有很大关系。所以我很想从这个想法最初是如何开始的开始。

paras.en: Newitz: So this is 100 percent me cribbing off my own nonfiction work. I published a book a couple of years ago called Four Lost Cities, which deals, in part, with Pompeii and how it was that the city was buried in ash, obviously, but also how people survived—because, in fact, one of the things that I think isn’t discussed very often is the fact that most of the people in the city were able to evacuate. There were, of course, many, many tragedies, and a lot of people did die. But it’s actually a really great example of what now we would consider to be, like, a modern rescue operation.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：所以这百分百是我抄袭我自己的非小说类作品。几年前，我出版了一本名为《四个失落的城市》的书，其中部分涉及庞贝古城，以及这座城市如何被埋在灰烬中，显然，也涉及人们如何幸存下来——因为，事实上，我认为不经常讨论的一件事是，城里的大多数人都能够撤离。当然，发生了很多很多的悲剧，确实有很多人死去。但这实际上是我们现在所认为的现代救援行动的一个很好的例子。

paras.en: And people resettled throughout the region, and I had spent an enormous amount of time thinking about Pompeii. I visited the city. I visited Herculaneum. I hung out with a lot of archaeologists—to the point where I’m sure I may have overstayed my welcome at their digs. And I kept thinking about the ordinary people who had lived at Pompeii, like, not the fancy people that we always hear about but just people who survived, who just did it by literally walking out of the city.
paras.zh: 人们在整个地区重新定居，我花了很多时间思考庞贝古城。我参观了这座城市。我访问了赫库兰尼姆。我和很多考古学家一起出去玩——以至于我确信我可能在他们的挖掘地停留得太久了。我一直在思考那些生活在庞贝古城的普通人，不是我们总是听到的那些奇特的人，而是那些幸存下来的人，他们只是通过真正走出城市来做到这一点。

paras.en: Newitz: And one of them is this woman, Murtis. We don’t know if she survived, but she did leave her name on the wall at the lupanar, the purpose-built brothel in the city. And there’s this really terrific scholar, Sarah Levin-Richardson, at the University of Washington, who’s written a lot about the lupanar and also the lives of sex workers.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：其中之一就是这个女人，穆蒂斯。我们不知道她是否幸存，但她确实把自己的名字留在了卢帕纳尔（lupanar）的墙上，卢帕纳尔是该市专门建造的妓院。还有一位非常出色的学者，华盛顿大学的莎拉·莱文-理查森 (Sarah Levin-Richardson)，她写了很多关于狼疮和性工作者生活的文章。

paras.en: And so she wrote this great article about Murtis and the graffiti that she left behind praising her own skills as a cocksucker, and why it was that we, kind of, know that women were leaving this graffiti. It wasn’t just, like, men saying things. And I kept wondering about Murtis. She sounded like someone that I would meet here in San Francisco who would be kind of ironically talking about how sexy she was. So I couldn’t let her go, and I finally was like, “All right. I need her to be one of the main characters in a novel.” And I brought her to life in this book, along with some of the other women who we know lived in Pompeii, like Julia Felix, who owned a massive shopping and bath complex, as well as a boarding house.
paras.zh: 因此，她写了这篇关于穆蒂斯和她留下的涂鸦的精彩文章，赞扬了自己作为混蛋的技巧，以及为什么我们知道女性会留下这些涂鸦。这不仅仅是男人说的话。我一直想知道穆蒂斯的事。她听起来就像我在旧金山遇到的一个人，她会讽刺地谈论她是多么性感。所以我不能让她走，最后我想，“好吧。我需要她成为小说中的主角之一。”我在这本书中将她和我们所知道的其他一些住在庞贝的女性一起栩栩如生地呈现出来，比如朱莉娅·菲利克斯，她拥有一个大型购物和浴室综合体，以及一个寄宿处。

paras.en: There’s some other women—like, Eumachia makes an appearance, for those of you who have the deep cut of knowing who that is. She’s another rich lady who left her name on a lot of buildings. And I’m a science-fiction writer, so it made perfect sense to me that the way we would meet Murtis would be a graduate student who is an alien slime mold who’s doing their fieldwork there in Rome.
paras.zh: 还有其他一些女性，比如 Eumachia 也出现了，对于你们这些深知她是谁的人来说。她是另一位在许多建筑物上留下自己名字的富婆。我是一名科幻小说作家，所以对我来说，我们会遇到穆蒂斯的方式是一个研究生，他是一个外星粘菌，正在罗马进行实地考察，这对我来说是完全合理的。

paras.en: And, actually, they don’t intend to be studying humans at all. They’re on Earth to study the ecosystem. They’re looking for single-celled organisms because they’re a single-celled organism. And so when they find humans, they’re kind of like, “What the heck is this?” [Laughs.]
paras.zh: 事实上，他们根本不打算研究人类。他们来到地球是为了研究生态系统。他们正在寻找单细胞生物，因为它们就是单细胞生物。所以当他们发现人类时，他们会想，“这到底是什么？” [笑。]

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Could you tell listeners who aren’t familiar with slime molds a little bit about why they’re so cool and interesting to us?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。你能告诉那些不熟悉粘菌的听众为什么它们对我们来说如此酷和有趣吗？

paras.en: Newitz: Wow. Okay. Well, so slime molds are kind of the charismatic microfauna, maybe, of the universe as we know it. So they’re not a fungus; they’re not a plant; they’re not an animal. They’re a protist, meaning, you know, they’re, like, kind of like amoebas. They’re more closely related to amoebas than, like, a fungus, even though we think of slimes and funguses as being kind of the same thing.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：哇。好的。好吧，粘菌可能是我们所知的宇宙中一种有魅力的微型动物。所以它们不是真菌；而是真菌。它们不是植物；他们不是动物。它们是原生生物，也就是说，它们有点像变形虫。尽管我们认为粘液和真菌是同一种东西，但它们与阿米巴原虫的关系比真菌更密切。

paras.en: And some slime molds, they exhibit a lot of the hallmarks of sentience. They can solve puzzles. You know, if you put them in a maze, and you put food outside the maze, they actually will solve the maze to get to the food.
paras.zh: 还有一些粘菌，它们表现出许多有知觉的特征。他们可以解决难题。你知道，如果你把它们放在迷宫里，然后把食物放在迷宫外面，它们实际上会解决迷宫以获得食物。

paras.en: Feltman: Right. I know there’s been some research looking at, like, using them to find the most efficient path or a layout for a network because they’re so good at finding food in mazes.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：对。我知道有一些研究正在研究，比如用它们来寻找最有效的路径或网络布局，因为它们非常擅长在迷宫中寻找食物。

paras.en: Newitz: Yeah. There was a paper about how slime molds may have solved the traveling salesman problem. And they also have these interesting life cycles where they go from being single-celled organisms to multicellular and back again sometimes. They’re a life-form that we barely understand. They’re very diverse, very beautiful but also sometimes super gross-looking to humans. I mean, I think they’re all very beautiful, but, you know, they’re slimy, especially when they group together in, in large quantities. So I think that what is exciting about them really is the fact that they seem to have these hallmarks of consciousness, even though they’re so different from us.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：是的。有一篇论文是关于粘菌如何解决旅行推销员问题的。它们也有这些有趣的生命周期，从单细胞生物到多细胞生物，有时又回到多细胞生物。它们是我们几乎不了解的生命形式。它们非常多样化，非常美丽，但有时对人类来说也非常丑陋。我的意思是，我认为它们都很漂亮，但是，你知道，它们很粘，尤其是当它们大量聚集在一起时。所以我认为他们真正令人兴奋的事实是他们似乎具有这些意识标志，尽管他们与我们如此不同。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah, so one of the things about your book that I think is such a delight and going to delight lovers of science fiction is that you clearly did so much work to have this character that is so alien, from a human perspective, be the point of view character and see Earth and humans as alien, as we would see this character.
