articles.title: Christian Pulisic showed up on Megan Moroney's lock screen picture after the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show

paras.en: Has Christian Pulisic moved up to lock screen picture material for Megan Moroney? That's the word on the street after the country singer's lock screen on her phone appeared to show the USMNT star.
This is round three of the dating rumors by my count, anyway. There was the rooftop bar sighting in Nashville and her trip to Italy that included her wearing what looked like one of his jerseys.

As someone who isn't up on all the lock screen protocols, I don’t know if a friend makes the cut or not. That said, it seems like it would be reserved for someone of more significance. But what do I know?

Moroney, after performing during the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, was leaving the event's after-party when the lock screen was spotted. You can see the picture of her leaving here and assign any significance you'd like to it.

I'd like to shift the focus, if I may, to something else that took place at the fashion show involving the singer. Yes, she made a dream of hers come true by performing a few songs on the runway, and that's great.
But it was a moment on the red carpet prior to the show that grabbed my attention. A heartwarming moment where she gave people a look at the person behind the persona.

It came with a simple story about overcoming an unexpected challenge. She was asked what was the most outrageous thing she's ever done in the name of fashion. Her answer involved another red carpet appearance.
"I’ll tell you what my brain immediately went to. The ACM Awards a few years ago, I had these like sticky underwear on, and they fell off on the carpet," Moroney told E News.
"Then I just took them off and gave them to my publicist. So yeah, I didn’t have underwear on, on the carpet. That’s outrageous."
It's outrageous. It's pushing through a difficult moment. It's human. It's storytelling. It's part of having yourself a huge night. Megan Moroney nailed this red carpet interview.

She then nailed her Victoria's Secret Fashion Show runway performance, even with enormous wings on, and topped it off with some Christian Pulisic fodder for those who spend their days in the celebrity rumor mill.
This is riding a media wave like a seasoned professional.

articles.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto

paras.en: Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement.
With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.
The Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, who grew up in Edmonton, Alberta’s capital, celebrated the result.
“Albertans made a clear choice. They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other. Above all, Albertans chose Canada.”

He said the result would allow Canadians to move forward together and accelerate efforts to diversify trade, develop major infrastructure projects and make Canada a global energy powerhouse, with Alberta at its centre.
The results showed an overwhelming majority of Albertans had voted to remain and one radio show host posted: “Someone owes Albertans $130m for this theatrical waste of taxpayers’ money.”
Pollster David Coletto told the Guardian that residents felt the referendum was “a distraction away” from what they wanted their government to focus on.

“There was almost a general sadness about the wasted energy spent on this rather than the more real threats they see, including the Trump administration,” he said. “Most Albertans feel deep grievances with the federal government while also being proudly Canadian. The marriage may be rocky at times, and most Albertans want to see some thing changed, but very few are willing to see the marriage end.”

The province’s separatists, however, saw a silver lining. “We don’t have the final results. I think the numbers are going to fluctuate, but it is fair to say that at least a quarter of Albertans feel that Alberta needs to be treated better,” said Keith Wilson, a leader of the separatist movement.

Others took a different view of the results. “The result is bleak. Independence feels far away and we should not pretend this was not a defeat, however, it changes nothing about the reality of the circumstances Albertans find themselves in,” David Parker, a longtime far-right organiser linked to a massive breach of voter information, wrote on social media.

The Alberta premier, Danielle Smith, welcomed the early results, saying they showed widespread support for remaining in Canada. “Albertans have voted for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada,” Smith posted on social media.

Even though the vote was not explicitly about independence – a point that frustrated separatists – the ballot question nonetheless exposed divisions in Alberta’s politics and raised questions about the durability of national unity.

Delays at roughly 100 of the 1,400 at polling stations across the province pushed results back by more than two hours, but shortly after polls closed on Monday evening the results suggested a decisive win for those looking to remain in Canada.

The separation question – whether to remain in Canada or begin a legal process that could lead to a second vote – was one of 10 put to Albertans on Monday. The others covered issues including immigration, healthcare, education and the province’s constitutional powers. Elections Alberta said the remaining results could take days to count.
In the days leading up to the vote, provincial leaders and federal politicians crisscrossed the province to make the case for a unified country.

Carney warned against a vote from residents of the oil-rich province simply looking to “send a message” to the federal government. “A vote against Canada is a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep uncertainty and lost opportunities for Albertans and Canadians,” he told an energetic crowd last week.
The Conservative leader, Pierre Poilievre, whose parliamentary seat is in the province, told a crowd of supporters that Albertans were not “quitters”.

“To those people who are thinking about taking out their frustration on the current government by voting for separation in the referendum, I say this: Canada is more than a government,” he said. “It is a people, a flag, a land, a history and a promise.”

Data from Elections Alberta indicated roughly 43% of eligible voters – or 1.3 million Albertans – had already cast ballots before Monday’s vote through advance voting and mail-in ballots. That figure pointed to a potentially higher turnout than the province’s last referendum in 2021.

Smith’s tenure as leader of the United Conservative party is due in large part to separatists within the party who ousted her predecessor, Jason Kenney. In recent months she has tried to placate both the separatists and federalists in the party, in a province where a majority is not interested in secession.
The referendum became a political liability for Smith’s party, whose popular support has tumbled in recent months, including with the loss of a one-time conservative stronghold in a by-election.

Still, members of the separatist movement told the Guardian they would continue their push for independence. And in the aftermath of the results, one prominent separatist leader said he would push for a special general meeting of the party to remove Smith.

Jeffrey Rath told Global News that the Alberta independence will remain nothing but a dream long as Smith, whom he called an “avowed federalist” remains in power. He said it was time for separatists to “take back ownership” of the UCP.

In an interview before the results, the Calgary mayor, Jeromy Farkas, a staunch opponent of the independence movement, said the city’s “best future is here, as a Canadian city”, amid fears that uncertainty could lead to capital flight.

“I am Canadian because I’m Canadian, not in a transactional way and regardless of the flavour of prime minister,” Farkas said. “And I’m going to continue to make the case for how our future is strongest together, because no result will permanently put this to bed. “The separatist movement sees this as a long-term project.”

articles.title: France’s culture of violent policing means the battle for its streets is far from over
articles.author: Jon Henley in Paris

paras.en: Familiar images of teargas clouds drifting across Paris squares, police baton charges against masked protesters and terrified teenagers floored – and worse – by stun grenades have once again focused the world’s attention on France’s policing methods.

While most of its western European neighbours generally favour police tactics that prioritise crowd containment and de-escalation, France has long responded to social movements that take to the streets with, at times, shocking physical force.

The reasons why are a complex mix of history, politics, state organisation and a particular security culture that has become deeply ingrained over decades, if not centuries, and whose limits continue to be pushed today.

French policing policy is rooted in Napoleon’s ultra-centralised state and in the political philosophy of the Republic. In France, the police are an instrument of the state. Their core task is to protect it, enforce its laws, and maintain public order.

Conceptually, that is a far cry from, for example, the UK, where since the early 1800s the police have been considered servants of the public, whose authority derives from public consent and whose chief responsibility is to keep the peace.

French police officers are agents of state authority. That means protests, blockades and mass disorder are not just civil nuisances, but direct challenges to the authority of the republic. The police’s priority is to reclaim the streets, not to negotiate.

That explains the aggressive tactics, such as systematically encircling and trapping crowds, and their continued use of “intermediate” or less-than-lethal weapons, many of which are banned or heavily restricted elsewhere in Europe.

Defence ball launchers, for example, fire rubber projectiles at 185mph (300kph). The explosive grenades that injured gilets jaunes protesters in the late 2010s and killed an environmental protester in 2014 have been phased out, but been replaced by pyrotechnic stun grenades.

Designed to disperse crowds through both impact and a 160dB acoustic shock, these have caused multiple injuries in recent years, including lost eyes and teeth, fractured jaws and several amputated limbs. They also frequently instil mass panic.

Violent policing methods are also fostered by France’s almost unique culture of street protest. A legacy of insurrection dating back to the 1789 revolution means protesters know the street can, and generally does, force governments to back down.

Unlike in Germany or the Netherlands, French unions, while they may strike often, are not formal government negotiating partners. The top-heavy, presidential structure of the Fifth Republic marginalises institutional consultation.

That means a heavily centralised state often passes laws with little popular agreement, making the “power of the street” one of citizens’ few viable means of forcing concessions. Protest here is regarded as a civic duty and a legitimate democratic tool.

That creates a vicious circle. French authorities see large crowds as an existential threat, so send in the police. Their military-style tactics entrench the aggression and alienate peaceful demonstrators. This prompts the more radical groups to opt for more violent tactics. But rather than isolating those elements, police respond with baton charges and munitions. And that turns protests into battles.

Data from conflict monitoring organisations, such as Acled, consistently shows that France, perhaps surprisingly, does not always record western Europe’s highest number of demonstrations (Germany and Italy also vie for that title).

But it does show that France consistently records the highest rates of escalated, high-intensity unrest, including street barricades, widespread vandalism and looting, arson attacks and direct confrontations between protesters and police.

France’s approach to policing and crowd management has for decades drawn condemnation from international human rights monitors and civil society groups, including Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and the Council of Europe.

Reports have documented instances of excessive force, misuse of grenades and rubber bullets, arbitrary mass arrests and routine teargas deployment against largely non-violent protesters. But the model persists, and is even expanding.

Last month, thousands marched in protest at a proposed “licence to kill” law seeking to establish a legal “presumption of self-defence” for police officers and gendarmes using firearms in the line of duty.

The law, opposed by civil rights groups, leftwing politicians, the magistrates’ union and the UN, would in effect shift the burden of proof on to victims and their families to demonstrate that a police shooting was disproportionate.

In essence, critics argue, it would institutionalise police impunity; reinforcing, once more, a security culture that treats public dissent and social tension not as democratic realities to be managed, but as insurrections to be repressed. The battle for France’s streets is far from over.

articles.title: US envoy Steve Witkoff to discuss proposals in Moscow after ‘positive’ meeting with Zelenskyy – Europe live
articles.author: Jakub Krupa (now) and Yohannes Lowe (earlier)

paras.en: Ukraine is thankful that intelligence on missile strikes 'works now,' Zelenskyy says
Zelenskyy says the talks covered security guarantees, among others, and he hopes to hear Russia’s response tomorrow.
He says Ukraine needs “strong security guarantees after the war ends.”
He also pointedly says that he is thankful that intelligence sharing “works now” (that’s my emphasis), and it helps with responding to any Russian attacks against Ukraine.
Ukraine is thankful that intelligence on missile strikes 'works now,' Zelenskyy says
Zelenskyy says the talks covered security guarantees, among others, and he hopes to hear Russia’s response tomorrow.
He says Ukraine needs “strong security guarantees after the war ends.”
He also pointedly says that he is thankful that intelligence sharing “works now” (that’s my emphasis), and it helps with responding to any Russian attacks against Ukraine.
Norway’s Støre jumps in to respond to a question on why Witkoff is not answering questions with the three other leaders.
He diplomatically points out that “this is a press conference among political leaders,” hinting that Witkoff is essentially of a different diplomatic rank.
But more broadly, he talks about the process, and the need for Europe “to be at the table.”
“To succeed, to achieve a last and fair piece, we need an equation of us, Ukraine, Russia and Europe and basically also other key countries, because this is a war with huge ramifications.”
He says he and Stubb don’t talk “on behalf of Europe,” but both countries, neighbours of Russia, have a deep understanding of the challenges faced by Europe.
Finland’s Stubb jumps in to add that they just work “in the back office” of the talks to support their progress.
He says Norway and Finland take part “because we believe in international law, but also based on self-interest” as Russia’s neighbours with “our history with Russia.”
“We’ll see what happens after tomorrow in Saint Petersburg. It’s very important that the American negotiators and President Trump stay engaged.”
Zelenskyy hints at further talks with US Rubio in the next 48 hours
Asked about his confidence in doing deal with Trump, Zelenskyy is very diplomatic.
He goes back to his conversation with Rubio earlier today, and says it was the right channel to discuss “sensitive issues” such as Stalink, interceptors, and intelligence sharing.
He says he hopes to talk with Rubio again in the next 48 hours.
In the Q&A, Ukraine’s Zelenskyy gets asked about his concessions and whether he is losing the war now.
He says the discussions revolved around “sensitive” issues, but he wants to “push as quick as possible to end this war” and focus next discussions on reconstruction.
He insists “we are not losing the war,” but concedes that “we are losing people and time,” as “our children do not have real life, childhood.”
He says “that is why we need to end this war as quick as possible.”
'Peace requires patience, but unfortunately war does not wait,' Stubb says as he hails 'genuine progress'
Finland’s Stubb says he believes today’s talks achieved some “genuine” progress “on two levels: … the short term and the big picture.”
“We found some elements of peace which will be taken forward to Saint Petersburg tomorrow.”
He says the discussions focused on “key issues such as air defence, energy installations, and partial ceasefires, such as those on energy and food security,” building on discussions in Miami.
Stubb says he understand “there has been a lot of noise” but “on a technical level, I feel that we are on the same page, and the next steps are about how we get there.”

“In my experience, peace requires patience, but unfortunately war does not wait. People are dying every day and each day. Our job is to do what we can to end it. And I think today was a step in the right direction.”
'Ukraine wants peace more than anyone,' Zelenskyy says as he calls for trilateral meeting with US, Russia
He thanks Norway for hosting the talks, and Finland’s Stubb for joining the process.
He says today’s talk with the US were “important” as he says all parties need to “keep talking at all levels and work together on the decisions needed to end this war.”
He thanks US secretary of state Marco Rubio for their earlier phone call conversation, too.
“Ukraine wants peace more than anyone. It was Russia who started this war, and the decision to keep the killing going is Russia’s choice and Russia’s alone.”

“We are working to find a solution. I thought we have some clear ideas on how to get to peace, and we are united with our European partners in this effort, and we want the Americans to take these ideas to the Russians.”
He says he wants a trilateral meeting of the leaders – that’s Trump, Putin and himself – because there are issues that “only the leaders” can resolve.
Norway’s Støre hails 'positive' meeting with Witkoff flying to Russia to discuss proposals tomorrow
He says Norway remains supportive of Ukraine, and “we have always made it clear there will be nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine.”
He thanks Trump’s envoys Witkoff and Kushner for joining the talks, and says:

“We believe that peace is possible and necessary for Ukraine and for Europe and for the entire world. We have hosted today, I would say, good and constructive talks, necessary after events of the last week. We have agreed that working together is crucial.”
He says US’s Witkoff will fly to St. Petersburg tomorrow to relay the result of today’s proposals to Russia, and “possibly pave the way for a meeting at the leaders’ level.”

“We have discussed today issues linked to security for Ukraine, prosperity plan after the war; issues related to territory and issues related to sanctions and questions related to European security order in the aftermath of this war.”
We are waiting for press conference after Ukraine-US talks in Oslo
We are now pausing our coverageas we wait for the Ukraine-US talks in Oslo to wrap up.
I will be back when the leaders of Ukraine, Norway and Finland show up for their press conference, which is currently expected around 6pm UK (7pm Oslo). We will bring you the presser live here.
In the meantime, here’s the summary of the day so far:

Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is in Oslo, holding talks with the US peace envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, with the Norwegian PM Støre and Finnish president Stubb also attending (12:23, 13:22, 16:06).

French authorities said that military forces will be deployed to reinforce “massive” police presence during the upcoming protests on Saturday (15:29, 15:57), as they framed the worsening situation as a choice between “violence and the Republic.”

Italian defence minister Guido Crosetto warned that city riots, seen also in the Italian city of Milan, are part of a broader “hybrid war” against the west, with younger people radicalising through the use of social media platforms (15:21), with the Italian government planning to approve new security measures (14:27).

EU trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the bloc’s relationship with the UK is of “vital importance in the current geopolitical, security and economic context,” as he set out the bloc’s expectations ahead of next month’s EU-UK summit on 20 November (11:44).
UN human rights chief condemns protests violence, worries about 'excessive use of force' by authorities

Meanwhile, UN Human Rights chief Volker Türk has condemned “all acts of violence” during the last week’s protests in Albania, Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal, and called on all parties to “reduce tensions and prevent further violence.”
In a statement he insisted that “the best and only way forward is inclusive and safe dialogue.”
“People have the right to protest peacefully, and to have their voices heard. States must facilitate these rights.
I deplore the actions of those exploiting protests to commit acts of violence and vandalism against public and private property. They should be held individually accountable.

I am concerned by reports of unnecessary and excessive use of force against protesters, including children. States must ensure that any law enforcement response remains lawful, necessary and proportionate. Allegations of unlawful use of force must be investigated promptly, effectively and independently, with accountability and effective remedies for victims.

I note some steps already taken by authorities to investigate incidents and ease tensions. I further urge States to engage protesters, particularly young people, in meaningful, inclusive and constructive dialogue, and to take concrete steps to address legitimate and fundamental human rights concerns over education, public services, housing, the rising cost of living and inequality.”
A short press release issued by the police quoted the head of investigation at the North Jutland force saying that “this is a case we are taking very seriously.”

The case focuses on suspected cooperation with foreign intelligence and has been brought forward in partnership with the Danish Security and Intelligence Service, the police said, without disclosing more detail.
The two men – which DR says are aged 18 and 21 – were arrested yesterday, and a preliminary court hearing is now getting under way.
But DR notes that the case is unusual given the hearing is taking place outside of regular court hours.
The incident comes less than a month after the Danish defence intelligence service issued a report warning against Russia’s activities.
For what it’s worth, we are expecting to hear from Zelenskyy, Stubb and Støre after today’s talks, probably around 6pm UK time (7pm Oslo).
We will bring you the key lines here, alongside a live stream to follow along.
In the last few minutes, Zelenskyy posted a video from today’s talks alongside the Norwegian and Finnish leaders, saying:
“Jonas, Alex, thank you for your unwavering support and DAILY attention to protecting lives. We are stronger together. Thank you, Norway! Thank you, Finland!”

articles.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say

paras.en: Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 300 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral.
paras.zh: 苏丹军队被指控发动了几次无人机袭击，据报道已造成300多人死亡，其中包括数十人前往参加葬礼。

paras.en: The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
paras.zh: 消息人士告诉苏丹战争观察站，周日晚上西科尔多凡州两个地区的罢工造成150人死亡，该观察站追踪了2023年军队和准军事快速支援部队（ RSF ）之间爆发的冲突。

paras.en: In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 153 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said.
paras.zh: 该地区信息部长表示，在苏丹和南苏丹之间有争议的阿卜耶伊边境地区，周一无人机袭击市场时造成153人死亡。

paras.en: A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF.
paras.zh: 一名军方消息人士告诉英国广播公司，军队进行了阿卜耶伊的袭击，称该市场是无国界医生的燃料供应点。

paras.en: The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011.
paras.zh: 这次袭击加剧了共同管理阿卜耶伊的南苏丹和苏丹之间的紧张局势，因为自2011年南苏丹割让以来，南苏丹和苏丹都声称对这一石油资源丰富的地区拥有所有权。

paras.en: South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest. There are fears the conflict could spill across the border.
paras.zh: 南苏丹已召集苏丹大使提出正式抗议。人们担心冲突可能会蔓延到边境。

paras.en: Despite a partial arms embargo on Sudan, foreign countries have been supplying both the army and the RSF with drones and they are increasingly becoming the weapon of choice in the conflict.
paras.zh: 尽管对苏丹实施了部分武器禁运，但外国一直在向军队和无人机部队提供无人机，它们越来越成为冲突中的首选武器。

paras.en: The war has created one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world, killed hundreds of thousands of people and forced more than 14 million from their homes.
paras.zh: 这场战争造成了世界上最严重的人道主义危机之一，数十万人丧生， 1400多万人被迫离开家园。

paras.en: "We are alarmed by the continued deadly drone strikes across the country that are killing civilians, including children, and that are disrupting essential services," UN spokesperson StÃ©phane Dujarric said on Monday, external.
paras.zh: “我们对全国各地持续的致命无人机袭击感到震惊，这些袭击正在杀害平民，包括儿童，并扰乱基本服务，”联合国发言人Stéphane Dujarric周一对外表示。

paras.en: The rising use of armed drones came as 20 million people faced acute hunger, with a rising risk of famine in parts of the western region of Darfur and Greater Kordofan, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，随着武装无人机的使用增加， 2000万人面临严重饥饿，达尔富尔西部地区和大科尔多凡州部分地区的饥荒风险上升。

paras.en: Greater Kordofan comprises three states and is a vital axis linking Darfur, controlled by the RSF, to the capital, Khartoum, now in army hands.
paras.zh: 大科尔多凡州由三个州组成，是连接无国界医生控制的达尔富尔和首都喀土穆的重要轴心，首都喀土穆现在由军队掌控。

paras.en: The wave of drone attacks started on Sunday evening and, according to the Sudan War Observatory, it is likely they were launched from the army-held city of Kadugli in South Kordofan state.
paras.zh: 无人机袭击浪潮始于周日晚上，根据苏丹战争观察站的数据，它们很可能是从南科尔多凡州军队控制的卡杜格利市发射的。

paras.en: A truck carrying around 200 mourners which had travelled from an area north of Abyei was hit as it arrived in the town of Al-Dabab in West Kordofan, the monitoring group said.
paras.zh: 监测组表示，一辆载有约200名哀悼者的卡车从阿卜耶伊以北地区开来，在抵达西科尔多凡州的Al-Dabab镇时被击中。

paras.en: Sources told the group that 145 people were killed and a tent where mourners at the funeral had gathered was also hit, killing five others. A further 150 people were injured in the attacks, it said.
paras.zh: 消息人士告诉该组织， 145人被杀，参加葬礼的哀悼者聚集的帐篷也被击中，另有5人死亡。它说，另有150人在袭击中受伤。

paras.en: Army drones also bombed a market in the town of Al-Mujlad in West Kordofan on the same evening, according to the Sudan War Observatory, which said the exact number of deaths and injuries were not yet known.
paras.zh: 据苏丹战争观察组织称，军用无人机当晚还轰炸了西科尔多凡州Al-Mujlad镇的一个市场，该组织表示，伤亡的确切数字尚不清楚。

paras.en: Sudan's army has not responded to the allegation it carried out these strikes, but said it did not attack civilians even if they believed there were RSF fighters amongst them.
paras.zh: 苏丹军队没有回应其进行这些罢工的指控，但表示即使他们认为平民中有无国界医生战斗人员，他们也没有袭击平民。

paras.en: The attack in Abyei, which borders West Kordofan, took place on Monday around 11:30 local time (09:30 GMT) targeting Amiet Market around 10km (six miles) from Abyei town, the region's Information Minister Yohana Akol Ngor told Radio Tamazuj, which broadcasts from the Netherlands to audiences on the Sudan-South Sudan border.
paras.zh: 与西科尔多凡州接壤的阿卜耶伊的袭击发生在当地时间周一11:30左右（格林尼治标准时间09:30 ） ，目标是距离阿卜耶伊镇约10公里（ 6英里）的Amiet市场，该地区的新闻部长Yohana Akol Ngor告诉Radio Tamazuj ，该电台从荷兰向苏丹-南苏丹边境的观众广播。

paras.en: On Tuesday, the minister confirmed to the Associated Press and Reuters that the death toll had risen from 73 to 153 people.
paras.zh: 周二，这位部长向美联社和路透社证实，死亡人数已从73人增加到153人。

paras.en: "It is a horrible and shocking situation," AP quotes him as saying.
paras.zh: “这是一个可怕而令人震惊的情况，”美联社援引他的话说。

paras.en: BBC Verify has studied satellite images that show extensive burnt buildings in the north-east corner of Amiet Market, which is also known in Arabic as Al-Na'am Market. Older images from the area show it is usually full of trucks.
paras.zh: BBC Verify研究了卫星图像，显示Amiet市场东北角有大量被烧毁的建筑物，该市场在阿拉伯语中也被称为Al-Na 'am市场。该地区的旧照片显示，它通常装满了卡车。

paras.en: It has also verified footage filmed near the market that shows a large plume of smoke, at least one petrol tanker and someone talking about five missiles being fired. Another verified video shows two massive, separate fires coming from buildings near that section of the market.
paras.zh: 它还核实了在市场附近拍摄的镜头，显示了大量烟雾，至少有一辆油轮和某人谈论正在发射五枚导弹。另一个经过验证的视频显示，该市场附近的建筑物发生了两起大规模的独立火灾。

paras.en: Earlier, Ngor told Reuters that emergency workers had struggled to retrieve the bodies because of fires caused by the strikes.
paras.zh: 早些时候，恩戈尔告诉路透社，由于罢工造成的火灾，紧急救援人员一直在努力找回尸体。

paras.en: On Monday, medical charity MÃ©decins Sans FrontiÃ¨res (MSF) said it had also received people wounded in the attack at Ameth Bek Hospital in Abyei town.
paras.zh: 周一，医疗慈善机构无国界医生组织（ MSF ）表示，它还在阿卜耶伊镇阿梅斯贝克医院（ Ameth Bek Hospital ）的袭击中接收了受伤人员。

paras.en: "So far we received over 20 patients, including several critical cases. Patients with burns were also admitted. We are providing surgical services and wound dressing, along with other emergency care," MSF's Christian Lindauer, the charity's manager at the hospital, said in a statement.
Meanwhile, a drone strike near the airport in Khartoum on Monday has killed four people, including three children, the AFP news agency reports, quoting a medical source.
It also cited a military source as saying air defences in the Sudanese capital had downed several other drones launched by the RSF towards the airport.
Fighting in Kordofan, a strategic area rich in gold and oil, has intensified over the last year after the army regained control of Khartoum from the RSF.

articles.title: Zelensky and US envoys holding Oslo talks as Rubio denies withholding intelligence

paras.en: US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Volodymyr Zelensky are meeting in Oslo, with relations on the slide between the Ukrainian leader and US President Donald Trump.
paras.zh: 美国特使史蒂夫·维特科夫（ Steve Witkoff ）和沃洛季米尔·泽伦斯基（ Volodymyr Zelensky ）正在奥斯陆会晤，乌克兰领导人和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（ Donald Trump ）之间的关系

paras.en: Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re said Zelensky had asked Oslo and neighbouring Finland to organise the talks with the US and European allies "at a critical time for Ukraine".
paras.zh: 挪威首相约纳斯·加尔·斯泰尔表示，泽伦斯基已要求奥斯陆和邻国芬兰“在乌克兰的关键时刻”组织与美国和欧洲盟友的会谈。

paras.en: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier rejected as "scandalous" accusations that Ukrainians were dying because the US was withholding intelligence from Kyiv.
paras.zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥（ Marco Rubio ）早些时候驳斥了关于乌克兰人因美国向基辅隐瞒情报而死亡的“丑闻”指控。

paras.en: He was speaking after Zelensky's top military adviser Serhii Beskrestnov told the BBC the lack of reliable US warnings - including about ballistic missile launches - meant lives were being lost.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基的高级军事顾问谢尔希·别斯克雷斯特诺夫（ Serhii Beskrestnov ）告诉英国广播公司，缺乏可靠的美国警告（包括有关弹道导弹发射的警告）意味着生命正在丧失。

paras.en: "This looks very strange," said Beskrestnov, widely known as "Flash". "Sometimes we receive this information before the attack, another time we [do] not."
paras.zh: “这看起来很奇怪，”贝斯克雷斯特诺夫说，他被广泛称为“闪电侠”。“有时我们在袭击前收到这些信息，另一次我们[没有]收到这些信息。”

paras.en: Relations between Kyiv and the US have soured in recent weeks to the extent that Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".
paras.zh: 最近几周，基辅和美国之间的关系恶化，以至于特朗普表示，现在是乌克兰选出新总统的时候了，最近一次是“让其他人代表乌克兰进行谈判”。

paras.en: Zelensky first met the Norwegian prime minister and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, ahead of his talks in person with Witkoff, with Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner taking part via video link.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基在与维特科夫亲自会谈之前，首先会见了挪威首相和芬兰总统亚历山大·斯图布（ Alexander Stubb ） ，特朗普的女婿贾里德·库什纳（ Jared Kushner ）通过视频链接参加了会谈。

paras.en: StÃ¸re said the aim of the talks was to steer relations towards "a more constructive path". He told reporters at the parliament in Norway that they wanted to ensure that the war ended diplomatically with a lasting and just peace.
paras.zh: Stáre表示，会谈的目的是引导关系走向“更具建设性的道路”。他在挪威议会告诉记者，他们希望确保战争在外交上以持久和公正的和平结束。

paras.en: Zelensky took with him to Oslo Ukraine's intelligence chief Rustem Umerov and influential lawmaker Davyd Arakhamia, both of whom had earlier this month held talks in Miami with Witkoff and Kushner.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基带着他去了奥斯陆乌克兰情报局局长Rustem Umerov和有影响力的议员Davyd Arakhamia ，他们本月早些时候在迈阿密与Witkoff和Kushner举行了会谈。

paras.en: Those talks were reportedly ended abruptly when the Ukrainian delegation learned that Trump had announced that Moscow would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to the US and other markets, bringing to an end American sanctions on Russian diesel exports.
paras.zh: 据报道，当乌克兰代表团得知特朗普宣布莫斯科将立即向美国和其他市场供应超过30万吨柴油时，这些谈判突然结束，从而结束了美国对俄罗斯柴油出口的制裁。

paras.en: Zelensky had reacted by calling it "a happy birthday present" for Russian President Vladimir Putin.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基的反应是称之为俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的“生日快乐礼物”。

paras.en: Ahead of next month's US midterm elections, Trump has blamed Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for fuel prices which have reached record highs at the pump since the start of the US-led war on Iran.
paras.zh: 在下个月的美国中期选举之前，特朗普将乌克兰对俄罗斯炼油厂的袭击归咎于自美国领导的伊朗战争开始以来油价创下历史新高。

paras.en: Speaking before the Oslo talks, Zelensky said he had had a "constructive discussion" with Rubio about the need for US early warnings, missile interceptors and SpaceX's Starlink internet network.
paras.zh: 在奥斯陆会谈之前，泽伦斯基表示，他与卢比奥就美国早期预警、导弹拦截器和SpaceX的Starlink互联网的必要性进行了“建设性讨论”。

paras.en: Last week a bipartisan group of US senators called for an urgent investigation into speed restrictions to the Starlink network in Ukraine. Unconfirmed reports on Tuesday said the transfer of more Patriot interceptors - the only effective weapon in shooting down Russian ballistic missiles - had not yet been approved.
paras.zh: 上周，一个由美国两党参议员组成的小组呼吁对乌克兰Starlink网络的速度限制进行紧急调查。周二未经证实的报道称，转移更多爱国者拦截器-击落俄罗斯弹道导弹的唯一有效武器-尚未获得批准。

paras.en: Rubio is currently on a visit to India and admitted to reporters that it may be true that Patriot interceptor missiles - the only had not yet arrived in Ukraine, although nothing had been denied to Kyiv intentionally.
paras.zh: 卢比奥目前正在访问印度，并向记者承认，爱国者拦截导弹可能是真的，这是唯一尚未抵达乌克兰的导弹，尽管基辅没有故意否认这一点。

paras.en: Zelensky was set to join his Norwegian and Finnish counterparts for a press conference after the talks, but Witkoff was not expected to join them, according to the government in Oslo, external.
paras.zh: 会谈结束后，泽伦斯基将与挪威和芬兰同行一起举行新闻发布会，但据奥斯陆政府表示，预计维特科夫不会加入他们的行列。

paras.en: It is not yet clear whether Witkoff will travel on to Russia after Oslo, however the Kremlin spokesman said he hoped a meeting with Trump's envoy could be organised in the near future. Dmitry Peskov said "we greatly appreciate the mediation efforts of the American negotiators".
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚维特科夫是否会在奥斯陆之后前往俄罗斯，但克里姆林宫发言人表示，他希望在不久的将来能够组织与特朗普特使的会晤。德米特里·佩斯科夫（ Dmitry Peskov ）说： “我们非常感谢美国谈判代表的调解努力。”

paras.en: European leaders have expressed concern about recent statements from the US towards Russia, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke on Monday of "mixed pictures and messages" on the war, adding that he was trying to convince the American government "in total that this is something we have to resolve jointly".
paras.zh: 欧洲领导人对美国最近对俄罗斯的言论表示担忧，德国总理弗里德里希·默茨（ Friedrich Merz ）周一谈到了有关战争的“混合图片和信息” ，并补充说，他试图说服美国政府“总的来说，这是我们必须共同解决的问题”。

paras.en: He pointed out that the US had not been paying for the defence of Ukraine since the start of 2025, and Europe and other countries were shouldering the burden.
paras.zh: 他指出，自2025年初以来，美国一直没有为乌克兰的国防付出代价，而欧洲和其他国家正在承担这一负担。

paras.en: "It's really a big effort for our budgets, it's really a big thing for the European Union, but we are doing that and we are trying to keep on doing that until this terrible war ends," the German leader told Bloomberg TV.
paras.zh: 这位德国领导人告诉彭博电视台： “这对我们的预算来说确实是一项巨大的努力，对欧盟来说确实是一件大事，但我们正在这样做，我们正在努力继续这样做，直到这场可怕的战争结束。”

paras.en: Asked whether or not Ukraine was a US ally, Vice-President JD Vance has said in a TV interview that Kyiv was "certainly a partner in some ways, but we have some divergent interests from time to time, like for example... I think they should stop bombing Russian energy".
paras.zh: 当被问及乌克兰是否是美国的盟友时，副总统JD Vance在接受电视采访时表示，基辅“在某些方面肯定是合作伙伴，但我们不时有一些不同的利益，例如......我认为他们应该停止轰炸俄罗斯能源”。

paras.en: "We don't have a formal alliance as far as I know with Ukraine. They're not in Nato, I don't think they should be in Nato... we're gonna work together on some things, but also we're going to be opposite on some things too."
paras.zh: “据我所知，我们与乌克兰没有正式的联盟。他们不在北约，我认为他们不应该在北约……我们会在一些事情上合作，但我们在一些事情上也会相反。”

paras.en: Russian drone attacks continued on Tuesday unabated. Ukrainian officials said at least 10 people were killed - four in Kyiv and the capital region, another four in the eastern Donetsk region, and two in the central city of Dnipro.
paras.zh: 周二，俄罗斯无人机袭击事件有增无减。乌克兰官员表示，至少有10人死亡，其中4人在基辅和首都地区， 4人在顿涅茨克东部地区， 2人在第聂伯罗市中心。

paras.en: In Kyiv, the operating room of a cardiology institute was hit, injuring one patient, Ukraine's Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky said.
paras.zh: 乌克兰总理谢尔希·科列茨基（ Serhiy Koretsky ）说，在基辅，一家心脏病研究所的手术室被击中，一名患者受伤。

paras.en: This comes a day after a Russian drone strike killed a toddler in her pram, an 11-year-old girl and another four people near a park cafÃ© in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
paras.zh: 此前一天，俄罗斯无人机袭击导致哈尔科夫东北部地区公园咖啡馆附近的一名婴儿、一名11岁女孩和另外四人死亡。

paras.en: Zelensky described that attack, in which another 14 people were injured, as "absolute atrocity".
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基称这次袭击是“绝对的暴行” ，另有14人受伤。

paras.en: Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
paras.zh: 普京于2022年发动了对乌克兰的全面入侵。

articles.title: 'Great result for Canada', says Carney as Alberta votes to reject separatism

paras.en: Prime Minister Mark Carney says an overwhelming vote by people in Alberta to remain part of Canada is a "great result" for the country.
paras.zh: 加拿大总理马克·卡尼（ Mark Carney ）表示，阿尔伯塔省人民以压倒性多数投票决定继续留在加拿大，这对该国来说是一个“伟大的结果”。

paras.en: Speaking to reporters as he walked into a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, Carney said he was "thrilled that Albertans have chosen unity" by rejecting a proposal to pursue separation through a binding referendum.
paras.zh: 卡尼在周二走进内阁会议时对记者说，他“很高兴艾伯塔人选择团结一致” ，拒绝了通过具有约束力的公投寻求分离的提议。

paras.en: Preliminary results indicate more than two-thirds chose Canada over a push for independence for the province, according to Elections Alberta, external.
paras.zh: 初步结果显示，根据艾伯塔省选举局的外部数据，超过三分之二的人选择加拿大而不是推动该省的独立。

paras.en: Monday's referendum was the result of a months-long campaign by separatists in the western Canadian province to get a public vote on the issue.
paras.zh: 周一的公投是加拿大西部省份分离主义者长达数月的竞选活动的结果，该活动旨在就此问题进行公众投票。

paras.en: Provincial leader Danielle Smith welcomed the initial results, commenting: "Albertans have voted for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada."
paras.zh: 省级领导人丹妮尔·史密斯（ Danielle Smith ）对初步结果表示欢迎，并评论说： “艾伯塔人投票赞成在一个统一的加拿大中建立一个更强大的艾伯塔省。

paras.en: Premier Smith herself opposed the separatist push but said the public will for a vote was undeniable, and many supporters of her own political party - United Conservative Party - were in the separatist camp.
paras.zh: 史密斯总理本人反对分离主义的推动，但表示公众的投票意愿是不可否认的，她自己的政党联合保守党的许多支持者都属于分离主义阵营。

paras.en: Smith said she would address Albertans later on Tuesday on the path forward for the province.
paras.zh: 史密斯说，她将在周二晚些时候就该省的前进道路向艾伯塔省人发表讲话。

paras.en: In making the case for independence from Canada, many of the separatists said the oil-rich province's economic growth had been stifled by the environmental policies of Canada's central government in Ottawa.
paras.zh: 在提出脱离加拿大独立的理由时，许多分离主义者表示，这个石油资源丰富的省份的经济增长受到加拿大中央政府在渥太华的环境政策的扼杀。

paras.en: But those who opposed a breakup - including Carney - called for Canada to present a united front in the face of external pressures, including an ongoing trade war with the United States.
paras.zh: 但包括卡尼在内的反对分裂的人呼吁加拿大面对外部压力，包括正在进行的与美国的贸易战，提出统一战线。

paras.en: "They've chosen to build together," Carney said. "They've chosen to continue to take care of each other, to move forward, to move forward together, with purpose, high ambition."
paras.zh: “他们选择了共同建设，”卡尼说。“他们选择了继续互相照顾，向前迈进，一起向前迈进，有目标，雄心壮志。”

paras.en: Carney added that he had spoken to Smith that morning and discussed "moving forward in the spirit of cooperative federalism, including on issues of immigration, other common priorities".
paras.zh: 卡尼补充说，他当天早上与史密斯进行了交谈，并讨论了“本着合作联邦制的精神向前迈进，包括移民问题和其他共同的优先事项”。

paras.en: Over the past year, the prime minister has worked with Smith on a number of shared goals, including pushing for an oil pipeline to the Pacific coast.
paras.zh: 在过去的一年里，总理与史密斯就一系列共同目标进行了合作，包括推动一条通往太平洋沿岸的石油管道。

paras.en: At a pro-separatist watch party in Edmonton, the hum of upbeat chatter quickly quieted as those present saw the projected results.
paras.zh: 在埃德蒙顿的一个支持分离主义的观察派对上，当在场的人看到预期的结果时，乐观的喋喋不休的嗡嗡声很快平静下来。

paras.en: After overnight vote projections were published by Canadian broadcaster CBC and others, the mood soured. The watch party attended by the BBC packed up quickly, and people went home.
paras.zh: 在加拿大广播公司CBC和其他机构发布隔夜投票预测后，情绪恶化。英国广播公司参加的观看派对收拾得很快，人们回家了。

paras.en: One of the separatist leaders, Jeffrey Rath, struck a defiant tone, however, vowing that "our movement isn't stopping and we're continuing to move forward".
paras.zh: 然而，分离主义领导人之一杰弗里·拉斯（ Jeffrey Rath ）发出了挑衅的语气，誓言“我们的运动不会停止，我们将继续前进”。

paras.en: Speaking to the BBC World Service's Newsday programme, Rath, a lawyer based in Calgary, said he saw Monday's vote as a "first step" which had taught the movement some "valuable lessons".
paras.zh: 总部位于卡尔加里的律师拉斯在接受英国广播公司世界服务新闻日节目采访时表示，他认为周一的投票是“第一步” ，这给该运动带来了一些“宝贵的教训”。

paras.en: Asked whether his movement would push to keep holding votes on independence until it got the result it wanted, he responded "why not?", and insisted that "the math and the economics" all added up on his side of the argument.
paras.zh: 当被问及他的运动是否会推动保持对独立的投票，直到获得想要的结果时，他回答说： “为什么不呢？” ，并坚持认为“数学和经济学”都在他的论点上。

paras.en: Premier Scott Moe, from the province of Saskatchewan, said he was glad Albertans chose unity, but added that "there is still work to be done on improving how Western Canada is treated by Ottawa".
paras.zh: 来自萨斯喀彻温省的省长斯科特·莫（ Scott Moe ）表示，他很高兴阿尔伯塔人选择团结，但他补充说， “在改善加拿大西部对待渥太华的方式方面仍有工作要做”。

paras.en: Pierre Poilievre, the leader of Canada's Conservative party and a member of parliament from Alberta, said on social media that "the promise of Canada is worth fighting for".
paras.zh: 加拿大保守党领袖、艾伯塔省议员皮埃尔·波利耶夫尔（ Pierre Poilievre ）在社交媒体上表示， “加拿大的承诺值得为之奋斗”。

paras.en: "Now our focus must be on results in people's lives: affordable food and homes, safe streets, strong borders, and less immigration," he said.
paras.zh: 他说： “现在，我们的重点必须放在人们生活的结果上：负担得起的食物和家园、安全的街道、强大的边界和较少的移民。”

paras.en: Smith called the vote after a grassroots group gathered about 300,000 signatures on a petition seeking a binding referendum on separation.
paras.zh: 在一个基层组织在一份寻求就分居问题进行具有约束力的公投的请愿书上收集了大约30万个签名后，史密斯召集了投票。

paras.en: The petition was blocked by a judge, saying it failed to consult indigenous First Nations people - however, Smith opted to go ahead with the ballot.
paras.zh: 法官阻止了这份请愿书，称请愿书没有征求土著原住民的意见，但史密斯选择继续进行投票。

paras.en: Another group collected signatures for its own petition that opposed separation, which was signed by more than 400,000 people.
paras.zh: 另一个团体为自己的请愿书收集了反对分离的签名，该请愿书有40多万人签名。

paras.en: The key question on Monday's voting paper asked: "Should Alberta remain a province of Canada or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?"
paras.zh: 周一投票文件中的关键问题是： “艾伯塔省应该继续是加拿大的一个省，还是艾伯塔省政府应该开始《加拿大宪法》要求的法律程序，就艾伯塔省是否应该从加拿大分离举行具有约束力的省级公投？”

paras.en: It's the first time a Canadian province has weighed the issue of separation since Quebec's two referendums, in 1980 in 1995.
paras.zh: 这是自1980年魁北克两次公投（ 1995年）以来，加拿大各省首次权衡分离问题。

paras.en: Both of those were unsuccessful, but Alberta separatists believe Quebec used the threat of independence to gain significant political leverage over Canada's central government.
paras.zh: 两者都不成功，但艾伯塔省的分离主义者认为，魁北克利用独立的威胁获得了对加拿大中央政府的重大政治影响力。

paras.en: Smith said before the vote that if Albertans chose the remain option, a binding referendum on separation would not be held - at least, not while she was in power.
paras.zh: 史密斯在投票前表示，如果艾伯塔人选择剩余的选择，就不会举行有约束力的分居公投-至少在她执政期间不会。

paras.en: Despite the projected results, the conversation around Albertan sovereignty is not over.
paras.zh: 尽管取得了预期的结果，但围绕阿尔伯塔主权的谈判尚未结束。

paras.en: Separatists leaders have indicated that they plan to try and push Smith out of power within her United Conservative Party, in the hope of installing a leader who is more sympathetic to their cause.
paras.zh: 分离主义领导人表示，他们计划试图将史密斯赶出她的联合保守党的权力，希望能够任命一位更同情他们事业的领导人。

paras.en: Another separatist leader, Mitch Sylvestre, told the BBC on polling day that "a lot of work will have to be done" to curb the appetite for independence if his side did lose.
paras.zh: 另一位分离主义领导人米奇·西尔维斯特（ Mitch Sylvestre ）在投票日告诉英国广播公司，如果他的球队输了， “必须做很多工作”来遏制独立的欲望。

paras.en: Although responses to the referendum question were tallied first, there were nine other non-binding questions on Monday's ballot paper.
paras.zh: 尽管对公投问题的回答首先进行了统计，但周一的选票上还有其他九个不具约束力的问题。

paras.en: Five of these dealt with immigration, while the other four focused on the Canadian constitution.
paras.zh: 其中五项涉及移民问题，而其他四项则侧重于加拿大宪法。

paras.en: Early results suggest that most will pass, including proposals for the province to take increased control over immigration levels.
paras.zh: 初步结果表明，大多数将通过，包括提议该省加强对移民水平的控制。

articles.title: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

paras.en: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

Have you ever wondered what enables everything from roaring construction machinery to agricultural machinery plowing the fields to industrial equipment shuttling through factories—the precise starting, smooth operation, and reliable braking they achieve?

The answer lies in a seemingly insignificant yet crucial core component: friction material. It acts as the "safety guard" and "power link" of machinery, ensuring every brake is safe and effective, and every power transmission is smooth and flawless.

Among the vast family of friction materials, wet friction materials are becoming the new favorite in modern machinery due to their exceptional reliability, safety, and exceptionally long lifespan. Among wet materials, paper-based friction materials stand out as a leading force thanks to their excellent overall performance, cost-effectiveness, and broad application prospects.
Today, let's delve deeper into the fascinating world of this "unsung hero"—paper-based friction materials.
What is Paper-Based Friction Material? — A Sponge-Like Power Core
Imagine a "sponge" with countless tiny pores—that's the most intuitive image of paper-based friction material.

It is a material with a reticular porous structure composed of three core components: reinforcing fibers, functional fillers, and a binder resin. This unique structure gives it extraordinary capabilities:
- Oil Storage Capacity: The porous structure acts like a miniature "oil depot," capable of storing large quantities of lubricant.

- Dynamic Lubrication: When the friction plate and mating plate engage and are subjected to pressure, the lubricant within the material is instantly squeezed onto the friction surface, forming a tough lubricant film, enabling smooth, gentle "wet" friction.
- Self-Recovery: When the friction plates separate, the material rebounds like memory foam, "absorbing" the lubricant back into the pores, ready for the next operation.

It is this dynamic cycle of "oil storage-oil squeezing-oil return" that allows paper-based friction materials to perform well in an oil bath environment, achieving a perfect combination of high durability and stable friction performance.
Exploring Core Performance: How Do Three Key Factors Affect It?

The performance of paper-based friction materials is not static. Like a top athlete, its performance is influenced by the "field," "equipment," and "condition." Let's examine how these three key factors shape its performance.
Factor 1: The "Stage Effect" of Lubricants

Paper-based friction materials are highly sensitive to lubricants, and different lubricants create distinct "stages" for their performance. Even the same friction material can exhibit significantly different friction characteristics (especially the kinetic friction coefficient) when exposed to different lubricants.
Figure 1: Kinetic friction coefficient curve for a paper-based friction material in gear oil
Figure 2: Dynamic friction coefficient curve of the same material in hydraulic oil

Interpretation: The above chart clearly shows that the same material behaves very differently in gear oil and hydraulic fluid. Furthermore, various additives added to lubricating oils (such as dispersants and anti-wear agents) can interact complexly with the material surface, further affecting its friction properties. Therefore, choosing the right oil for paper-based friction materials is the first step in achieving optimal performance.
Density is a trump card for paper-based friction materials. It is directly related to the material's porosity, leading to a delicate balancing act in terms of performance.

High density (low porosity) means a denser material, resulting in better strength and thermal conductivity, lower wear rate, and longer life. However, the downside is reduced oil storage capacity, which can lead to a lower coefficient of friction and compromise power transmission.

Low density (high porosity) means the material is more porous, resulting in greater oil storage capacity and a higher coefficient of friction, which can provide greater braking force or transmit torque. However, the downside is reduced mechanical strength and wear resistance, shortening service life.
Figure 3: Comparison of the dynamic coefficient of friction for materials of varying densities (Type 2 to Type 6, increasing density)
Figure 4: Comparison of wear rates of materials with different densities

Interpretation: Figures 3 and 4 vividly illustrate this balancing act. There's no such thing as absolute good or bad, only suitability. When selecting a paper-based friction material, the optimal trade-off between friction coefficient and durability must be determined based on specific application requirements (e.g., high torque versus long life).
Factor 3: Extreme Challenges of Operating Conditions

In addition to oil type and density, actual operating conditions, such as surface pressure, sliding speed, and oil temperature, pose extreme challenges to paper-based friction materials. These factors directly affect the temperature of the friction interface, the thickness and stability of the oil film, and thus dynamically alter the coefficient of friction.

Therefore, please remember: the coefficient of friction of a particular paper-based friction material is not a fixed value, but rather a performance range determined through extensive and repeated testing under specific operating conditions.
Broad Applications: Injecting a Powerful "Heart" into Machinery

Thanks to its excellent overall performance and customizability, Carlisle Brake & Friction's paper-based friction materials have been successfully applied to the core components of various heavy-duty machinery, becoming their powerful and reliable "heart."
We understand that different machines and applications require significantly different friction materials. For example:
- Service brakes for construction machinery (such as excavators and loaders) require materials that provide a stable, powerful braking force under high loads to ensure safety.
- Powershift transmissions for agricultural machinery (such as tractors) require materials that provide smooth engagement and excellent heat resistance to handle frequent shifting.
- Clutches for industrial machinery require materials that respond quickly and have a long lifespan to ensure continuous and efficient operation of production lines.

To this end, Carlisle Brake & Friction has developed a series of special paper-based friction materials for different application scenarios, providing each customer with the most suitable and reliable solution.
Continuous Innovation, Driving the Future
Technological advancement is endless. To meet increasingly demanding application requirements and broaden market prospects, Carlisle Brake & Friction remains at the forefront of innovation.

We are not only continuously optimizing the formulation and processing of paper-based friction materials to push their performance limits, but are also actively exploring next-generation wet friction materials with even higher performance. These R&D efforts have made significant progress, aiming to provide global customers with more diverse and advanced options, driving the infinite possibilities of future machinery.

articles.title: Celebrating 100-Years with Medina Mayor and Employees

paras.en: Celebrating 100-Years with Medina Mayor and Employees

MEDINA, OHIO — September 24, 2025 — Carlisle Brake & Friction (CBF), a global leader in the development and manufacture of high-performance brake and friction solutions, today welcomed Medina Mayor Dennis Hanwell, Economic Development Director Kimberly Marshall, and Executive Director of the Medina Chamber of Commerce Jaclyn Ringstmeier, for a special photo op at the company’s headquarters, located at 920 Lake Road. The event was a commemorative celebration of CarlisleCBF’s 100-year anniversary and its enduring presence in the Medina community.

paras.en: The photo op featured Mayor Hanwell alongside Carlisle’s Operations Leader, David Smith, and a number of employees who have been with the company for decades. The occasion honored CarlisleCBF’s century of innovation and its deep roots in the Medina area, where it has been a significant employer and community partner.

"We are incredibly proud of our history and our strong connection to the city of Medina," said David Smith. "This milestone is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our employees, many of whom have been with us for decades. We are grateful for the continued support of Mayor Hanwell and the entire Medina community."

The photo op followed a recent employee and family event at the Medina plant that celebrated the 100-year milestone. The celebration was filled with games, face painting, food, and fun for all ages, reinforcing the company's commitment to its employees and their families.

Mayor Hanwell expressed his gratitude for CarlisleCBF’s presence in the city. “Carlisle has been a part of the Medina community for nearly 65 years, providing good jobs and a strong economic foundation,” said Mayor Hanwell. "We are proud to celebrate their 100-year anniversary and recognize the significant role they have played in our city’s growth and prosperity."
CarlisleCBF, a brand of CentroMotion, was founded in 1925 and has grown to become a global leader in its field, serving a wide range of markets including agriculture, construction, and mining.

Carlisle Brake & Friction, a CentroMotion brand, is a leading global provider of highly engineered and integrated brake and friction solutions for a wide range of industrial applications. With over 100 years of experience, the company is dedicated to delivering innovative, reliable, and high-performance products to its customers worldwide.

articles.title: Autel Leads Where It Counts: Access
articles.author: Autel

paras.en: For collision shops investing in ADAS equipment and training, access to protected vehicle systems is essential to putting that investment to work. Technicians need to communicate with the vehicle, perform the required procedures and document the results before a repair is complete.

Autel continues to expand those capabilities through software development, secure gateway access and improvements shaped by technician feedback. Across supported Stellantis, Nissan, Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen/Audi vehicles, that work gives appropriately equipped shops more opportunities to perform diagnostics and ADAS calibrations in-house.
The benefit is practical: greater control over scheduling, fewer handoffs and more opportunities to put the shop’s equipment and technician expertise to work.

Security gateways protect vehicle systems by restricting certain diagnostic and service functions to authenticated users. For an independent shop, having a compatible diagnostic tool and calibration equipment is only part of the equation. Access to protected functions can determine whether the technician can complete the job.

Autel provides secure gateway access for supported Stellantis, Nissan and Mercedes-Benz vehicles through AutoAuth, an online service that authenticates registered shops and technicians. Supported Volkswagen and Audi SFD access is available directly through compatible Autel tablets.
Depending on the vehicle, system and tool, authenticated access enables protected operations such as clearing codes, performing Active Tests and initiating supported ADAS calibration procedures.

Shops should confirm vehicle-specific coverage and account requirements before scheduling the work. Maintaining the applicable Autel software subscription, authorization service account and internet connection helps technicians arrive prepared to access the functions they need.
Autel’s work to expand secure access spans multiple vehicle manufacturers and years of development.

In June 2020, Autel introduced AutoAuth-based gateway access for supported Fiat Chrysler Automobiles vehicles, now part of Stellantis. Nissan Central Gateway access through AutoAuth followed in May 2024. By December 2024, Volkswagen/Audi SFD access was available directly through compatible Autel tablets.

Autel announced initial Mercedes-Benz security-gateway access through AutoAuth in January 2025, followed that July by enhanced access for additional protected operations on select 2021 and newer models, including supported ADAS calibrations.

“With access to this enhanced gateway, Autel users can now perform additional services, including ADAS calibrations, on the latest Mercedes vehicles,” said Paul A. Marshall, Director of Product Development for Autel U.S., when the company announced the capability in July 2025.
Further Nissan software development has expanded supported diagnostic and calibration functions on eligible MaxiSYS tablets, adding more late-model applications to the work shops can perform.
Each expansion serves the same purpose: helping independent technicians access the vehicle functions required to complete supported repairs.
Access becomes valuable when technicians can use it successfully on the vehicles in front of them. That requires compatible equipment, clear instructions and careful preparation.

Autel’s calibration software presents vehicle-specific setup guidance to help technicians prepare the vehicle, position the equipment and follow the applicable procedure. Accurate calibration depends on meeting requirements for vehicle condition, target placement, working environment and verification.

On Autel’s optical positioning systems, software safeguards require verified setup measurements to fall within specified tolerances before technicians can proceed. These checks help identify positioning problems before calibration begins and reduce the risk of failure caused by incorrect setup.

Autel also continues to develop equipment for different shop environments and service models. The MA800 mobile calibration system, for example, combines laser-guided positioning with independent pitch, roll and yaw adjustment to help technicians establish the required target position.
Together, vehicle access, setup guidance and calibration equipment help shops turn supported coverage into completed work.
Completing a calibration also means documenting what was done.

Autel’s scan reports and calibration records help shops communicate diagnostic findings and procedure results to estimators, customers, insurers and others reviewing the repair. Keeping those records with the job supports a clearer account of the work performed.

Autel continues to refine its reporting based on feedback from collision repair shops, mobile service providers, ADAS calibration businesses and technicians. That feedback helps guide improvements to the information available to both the person performing the work and the person reviewing it.

As vehicle technology advances, shops need tools that continue to improve with it. Expanded access, broader coverage, clearer procedures and useful documentation all contribute to the value of their equipment investment.

Autel’s commitment extends across research, engineering and technician education, with a focus on helping shops perform supported work accurately and efficiently. The technicians using these tools every day remain central to that effort: their experience helps identify what needs to improve and where development can make the greatest difference in the repair bay.
For collision shops, that commitment means more opportunities to keep work with the team responsible for the repair—and greater confidence in the tools supporting it.
Learn more at autel.us/security-gateways.

articles.title: SCRS OEM Summit: GM, Ford, Rivian engineers on importance of ADAS repair procedures
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: The Society of Collision Repair Specialists (SCRS) has shared details about the third and final session of its 2026 OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit, which will wrap up an afternoon program focused on vehicle safety, from national objectives to vehicle engineering and into the collision repair process.

“Preserving the Safety System: Sensors, Calibration and Repairability” will take place Thursday, Nov. 5, from 3:30–4:30 p.m. during the SEMA Show in Las Vegas, featuring ADAS systems and service engineering experts from General Motors, Ford Motor Co., and Rivian.
SCRS says the session will answer for repairers what it takes to preserve and restore the ADAS safety capabilities engineered into the vehicle after collisions.

“Cameras, radar, and other sensing technologies are fundamentally changing what vehicles can understand about the environment around them,” an SCRS press release states. “These systems can identify objects, measure distance and velocity, recognize roadway conditions, and combine information from multiple sensors to support increasingly sophisticated vehicle decisions. That capability also introduces extraordinary precision into the collision repair process.”

The third OEM Summit session will bring together the GM, Ford, and Rivian engineers who are responsible for sensing systems, vehicle performance, calibration strategies, and service engineering so they can discuss what today’s sensors can do, what can affect their performance, and how automakers translate engineering requirements into repair procedures and field instructions.

- Steven Vance, principal hardware engineer, engineering technical leader, and ADAS sensors and sensing systems at GM — among his responsibilities are sensor capabilities and requirements that affect repair, including sensor modalities and strengths, the importance of sensor alignment, and the potential influence of aftermarket accessories on sensing performance.

- Chad Zagorski, principal systems engineer and ADAS at GM — develops new ADAS technologies and improves existing systems, focusing on enhancing ADAS performance across GM’s vehicle lineup. His work combines engineering and product development with industry collaboration on standards and test-method development.

- Brian Perkins, body and damageability commodity manager of design for service at Ford — leads Ford’s collision and damageability team and oversees the Paint and Body Technology Center. His team represents collision repair technicians within Ford’s global organization by testing and validating repair tools and procedures. SCRS says this work ensures that technicians have the information necessary to properly repair Ford vehicles, including increasingly important ADAS documentation.

- Ryan Davenport, service engineering, propulsion and electronics senior manager at Rivian — oversees service program launches, ADAS and propulsion diagnostics, and incident resolution. His work includes troubleshooting complex vehicle systems, ensuring Rivian’s electric vehicles meet service and safety requirements, and improving the technician and customer experience.

SCRS says the panelists will explore how sensors are designed to operate and how variables introduced by a collision or repair, such as sensor position, mounting locations, structural dimensions, wheel alignment, ride height, replacement glass, body materials, and other seemingly small changes, can affect what a vehicle’s sensing systems perceive.
The discussion, moderated by Database Enhancement Gateway (DEG) Administrator Danny Gredinberg, will also take attendees behind the development of collision repair information to cover:
- How engineering requirements become service procedures;
- How calibration strategies are established and tested; and
- What a successful calibration actually verifies about system performance.

“Those questions grow increasingly significant as crash avoidance and mitigation technologies play a larger role in vehicle safety,” the release states. “The session will ultimately confront a question with direct implications for every business repairing modern vehicles: what must a collision repair facility do to confidently determine that a vehicle’s safety systems have been restored to the performance its manufacturer intended?”

SCRS says together, the three 2026 OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit sessions are designed to tell a connected story about vehicle safety: “What safety outcomes is the nation trying to achieve? How are those outcomes engineered into the vehicle? And after a collision, how do we preserve them?”

For collision repair professionals working on modern vehicles, SCRS encourages attendees to participate in the entire series rather than viewing the sessions independently. To register for the entire summit, click here.

The afternoon begins with “The National Safety Objective: Safer Vehicles, Safer Roads,” featuring National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) Deputy Administrator Lee White, who will examine federal vehicle and roadway safety priorities.

The second session, “Engineering the Safety Benefit: From Requirement to Real-World Performance,” features safety and ADAS engineering leaders from General Motors, who will explore how automakers translate safety objectives into vehicle technologies. It will also cover how they establish performance requirements and evaluate whether those technologies produce measurable safety benefits in the real world.

Panelists will include Michael Carpenter, General Motors Active Safety and Global Vehicle Performance owner; Jameson Collins, General Motors Active Safety and staff product manager; and Jeremy Nelson, Ford Motor Co. ADAS application systems engineer.
The 2026 OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit is part of SCRS’ Repairer Driven Education (RDE) program at the SEMA Show, which includes several classes, the IDEAS Collide Showcase, and more.

An SCRS RDE Full Series Pass provides access to Tuesday and Wednesday RDE sessions, IDEAS Collide, the OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit, and the SCRS Afterparty. To register for the full series pass, click here.
For additional information about SCRS and Repairer Driven Education, visit scrs.com/rde.

articles.title: CCC: Mid-year collision repair trends update show more expensive claims, total losses
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: A mid-year update to CCC Intelligent Solutions’ 2026 Crash Course report on industry trends and repair data shows higher-cost claims, older vehicles driving up total losses, technology-rich newer vehicles, and consumers with less financial flexibility.
CCC’s report states that claims frequency was down 3.5% through September compared with an 8.3% decline through the same period in 2025.
Repairable estimates declined 5.4%, compared with a 10.4% decrease a year earlier. Total loss valuations increased 1.1% after declining 3.1% through September 2025.
Non-comprehensive repairable claims decreased 4.2%, compared with an 8.9% decline a year earlier. Total loss valuations increased 1.4% after declining 1.2% through September 2025.

CCC notes that the composition of changes in claim volume shifted somewhat in 2026, with collision and comprehensive claims accounting for 80% of total volume reduction, compared with about 90% in 2025.

“First-party filings continue to be influenced by increased deductibles, premium sensitivity, and consumers’ willingness to absorb smaller losses themselves,” CCC writes. “The result is a system processing fewer claims, but a mix increasingly concentrated toward losses that are less discretionary.”

The share of driveable vehicles deemed total losses reached 11.2% through the first half (H1) of 2026, up from 10.3% a year ago, and 6.3% in 2022. CCC writes that, historically, over 80% of all driveable vehicles deemed total losses are seven years old or older. Non-driveable total loss frequency also increased to 52.5% in H1 across all loss categories.
CCC says repair cost inflation flattened in H1.
The average total cost of repair (TCOR) reached $4,821 in H1, 0.6% above H1 2025.
“This is a significant deceleration from the 15.7% increase recorded in H1 2022,” CCC writes. “Since 2020, however, the average has still risen from approximately $3,331 to more than $4,800.”
CCC adds that average part prices remained 8% higher year over year through early 2026, while labor rates increased by 1.5%.

“The increases in average price per part are generally aligned with tariff activity, the landscape of which continues to evolve in 2026,” CCC writes. “Most notably, the White House has announced 50% tariffs on Canadian automobiles and auto parts under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, beginning January 1, 2027. If they are implemented like current Section 338 measures, they would apply in addition to existing duties, with no exemption for USMCA-qualifying goods.”

While repair inflation has normalized, CCC says the underlying cost base remains more than 40% above 2020 levels. According to CCC, 27% of Q1 non-comprehensive claims included more than 15 parts, and fewer than 32% exceeded 30 labor hours. And both measures were shifting toward less-intensive repair bands.
Higher insurance deductibles have also become the norm, according to CCC’s findings.
Repairable collision claims carrying deductibles of $1,000 or more reached 28.4% in H1, up from 25.7% a year ago and 20.3% in H1 2022.

“For consumers, a higher deductible can provide immediate premium relief,” CCC writes. “For the claims ecosystem, it changes the economics of filing. A $1,000 (or higher) deductible makes relatively minor damage easier to postpone, self-fund, or leave unrepaired. That removes smaller claims from the population and raises the apparent severity of those that remain, not to mention exacerbating the share of total losses.
“H1 2026 data suggests that affordability-driven coverage decisions are becoming embedded in the claims mix rather than representing a temporary response to premium increases.”

CCC notes findings from a recent VIU by Hub Insurance survey: 67% of policyholders said covering a $1,000 unexpected home or auto expense would be a struggle, with about 1 in 5 of them (21%) calling it “a serious hardship” or “significant struggle.”
CCC says the first half of the year also brought total loss frequency to another high.

Through Q2, 23.5% of claims across all loss categories were flagged as total losses, up 0.8 percentage points year over year. Non-comprehensive total loss frequency reached 24.1%. CCC says that means both results extend the climb from the 2022 lows of 18.2% and 19.4%, respectively.

“Higher total loss frequency is partly a product of loss economics, but filing behavior also affects the denominator,” CCC writes. “When lower-severity first-party claims are not reported, fewer small repairable claims remain to dilute the total loss share. The customer implications are material. CCC’s Moments of Truth study found that 40.4% of insureds with a confirmed total loss switched carriers, compared with 7.6% following a repairable claim. As personal auto competition increases, total loss handling becomes not only an operational challenge but also a retention issue.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The mid-year update touches on the aging vehicle fleet as well, which CCC says is now visible throughout the loss mix. CCC writes that vehicles seven years or older represented 74.3% of total loss valuations in H1 2026, with vehicles between seven and 12 years old accounting for 41%, compared with 33.4% in 2020.

“An older fleet does not automatically mean a simpler claim,” CCC writes. “Older vehicles carry lower adjusted values and can cross total loss thresholds quickly, even after damage that leaves them operable. At the same time, many still contain technology that requires diagnostics or specialized procedures.”

CCC also found that self-pay repair is becoming “a meaningful parallel market,” representing 26% of repair orders in H1 2026, up 0.5 percentage points year over year. The average ticket was $1,941. By comparison, CCC says the average repairable insurance claim was $4,821 and more than 71% of self-pay orders were below $2,000, while 75% of insurance repairable claims exceeded that amount.
The report also touches on diagnostics trends in collision repair and the hybrid and electric vehicle segments.
In Q1 2026, CCC says 74.8% of repairable appraisals included a scan and 29.9% included a calibration, up from 70.9% and 23.3%, respectively, a year ago.
Among DRP appraisals, scan penetration reached 89.8% and calibration penetration reached 40.6%, according to CCC.

“More than 83% of industry scans appeared on the initial estimate, while 47% of calibrations were captured there,” CCC writes. “For DRP claims, 93.1% of scans and 50.9% of calibrations appeared on the initial estimate. This suggests diagnostics are becoming less of an exception discovered later in the repair and more of a recognized requirement at intake.”

Regarding hybrid vehicles, CCC says they represented 9.9% of repairable claims in Q2 across all vehicle ages compared with 4.3% for electric vehicles. Among vehicles three years old or newer, the hybrid share reached 19.0%, while EVs were 9.5%.

For vehicles three years old or newer, average hybrid TCOR reached $6,415 — $435 below the EV average of $6,850. Since 2020, CCC says hybrid repair costs have increased 53.6%, compared with 16.3% for EVs. EVs remain the most expensive fuel type in this age group, according to CCC.
To view the 2026 Crash Course report, released in March 2026, click here.

articles.title: BendPak Launches Ranger DST30PX Balancer
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Ranger Division of BendPak has introduced the next-generation DST Series wheel balancer, the DST30PX. As shops face larger OEM wheel assemblies and heavy aftermarket truck tires, older balancing platforms can slow production. The DST30PX is built to handle oversized wheels and prevent bottlenecks with a new hood design, larger shaft and overhauled structural chassis.

The hood accommodates a wider range of tire shapes and sizes, including oversized off-road and fleet tires, without repositioning. An open-side design allows wider tires, aggressive offsets and bulky sidewalls to slide in more easily, reducing setup time and enabling operators to position wheel assemblies up to 43 inches in diameter.

Ranger reinforced the chassis and hood assembly to handle the added mass of larger assemblies without flexing, compromising alignment or generating excess vibration. The added rigidity helps maintain consistent measurements for accuracy. A 40 mm shaft increases stiffness and accuracy for heavier wheels while supporting standard cones and accessories.

“The Ranger DST30PX represents a fundamental shift in how modern shops handle today’s radically heavier, oversized wheel configurations,” said Sean Price, director of product development for BendPak Inc. “By optimizing the physical layout and integrating a high-precision sensor array, we ensure technicians can mount, spin and perfectly balance oversized assemblies without a single second of wasted motion — turning massive wheel packages into a rapid, routine six-second floor-to-floor operation.”

The DST30PX features a 64-tooth magnetic transducer encoder with precision-cut square teeth to convert rotary position into a digital electronic signal, helping achieve accurate profile readings and top-dead-center positioning for precise weight placement. The extra encoder resolution supports cleaner correction, smaller weight changes and better placement accuracy for performance wheels, larger tiresand customers sensitive to vibration.
User-friendly Design for Fast Turnarounds

The DST30PX streamlines repetitive wheel service by reducing unnecessary motion. Simple wheel data entry, precise rolling weight readings, automatic braking, manual or automatic hood-start operation, and a rapid cycle time help technicians balance more wheels with fewer errors.

A quick-release hub nut, side-position brake, top-dead-center weight indicator, and tiered placement indicators accelerate setup and correction. Onboard storage includes a high-volume top tray, side cone pegs, and a side shelf designed to accommodate Ranger Quick-Peel adhesive tape weight rolls.
- 145-lb. capacity, 30-in. wheel diameter range, and 43-in. max tire diameter
- Low-RPM balancing operation and six-second cycle time
- Dynamic, Static and Performance Alloy settings
- 16-bit processor and multi-directional quartz piezoelectric sensors
- Ergonomic controls and full-tilt LED display control panel
- Automatic braking and self-calibration

The DST30PX is positioned as an upgrade for shops seeking higher precision, faster workflow and an advanced measuring system for modern wheels without moving to a larger machine.
